18.4.67.a.m: Those who undertake this: an atirātra, a thousand years of trivṛt agniṣṭomas, [and] an atirātra.

18.4.68.a.s: viśvasṛjām̐ sahasrasaṃvatsaraṃ viśvam enān anusṛjate / ya etad upayanti pañcapañcāśatas trivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarāḥ pañcapañcāśataḥ pañcadaśāḥ pañcapañcāśataḥ saptadaśāḥ pañcapañcāśata ekavim̐śāḥ / viśvasṛjām̐ sahasrasaṃvatsaram / viśvam enān anusṛjate / ya etad upayanti / tatra śloko viśvasṛjaḥ prathamāḥ satram āsata sahasrasamaṃ prasutena yantaḥ / tato ha jajñe bhuvanasya gopā hiraṇmayaḥ śakunir brahmanāmeti / tatra brahmaṇaḥ sāyujyam̐ salokatām yanti ya etad upayanti ya etad upayanti //
18.4.68.a.d: विश्वसृजाम्̐ सहस्रसंवत्सरं विश्वम् एनान् अनुसृजते । य एतद् उपयन्ति पञ्चपञ्चाशतस् त्रिवृतः संवत्सराः पञ्चपञ्चाशतः पञ्चदशाः पञ्चपञ्चाशतः सप्तदशाः पञ्चपञ्चाशत एकविम्̐शाः । विश्वसृजाम्̐ सहस्रसंवत्सरम् । विश्वम् एनान् अनुसृजते । य एतद् उपयन्ति । तत्र श्लोको विश्वसृजः प्रथमाः सत्रम् आसत सहस्रसमं प्रसुतेन यन्तः । ततो ह जज्ञे भुवनस्य गोपा हिरण्मयः शकुनिर् ब्रह्मनामेति । तत्र ब्रह्मणः सायुज्यम्̐ सलोकताम् यन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति य एतद् उपयन्ति ॥
18.4.68.a.m: For the thousand-year [session] of the Viśvasṛjs, the universe creates itself after them. Those who undertake this: fifty-five years are trivṛt; fifty-five are pañcadaśa; fifty-five are saptadaśa; fifty-five are ekavim̐śa. For the thousand-year [session] of the Viśvasṛjs, the universe creates itself after them, who undertake this. On this there is a verse: / 'The Viśvasṛjs were the first to sit for a sacrificial session, proceeding with pressed [soma] for a thousand years. / Thence was born the protector of the universe, the golden bird, named Brahman.' / There, those who undertake this, who undertake this, go to union and co-residence with Brahman.

21.0.1.a.s: devā yo apsu mahima iṣavaḥ sa
21.0.1.a.d: देवा यो अप्सु महिम इषवः स
21.0.1.a.m: devā yo apsu mahima iṣavaḥ sa [...]

21.0.1.b.s: idam āpaḥ pravahata \ yat kiṃca duritaṃ mayi / \ yac cāham abhidudroha \ yac ca śepa udākṛtam //
21.0.1.b.d: इदम् आपः प्रवहत \ यत् किंच दुरितं मयि । \ यच् चाहम् अभिदुद्रोह \ यच् च शेप उदाकृतम् ॥
21.0.1.b.m: Carry away, O Waters, whatever evil is in me, / and whatever I have acted maliciously against, and whatever I have sworn, lifting up water.

21.0.1.c.s: bhūḥ prapadye \ bhuvaḥ prapadye \ suvaḥ prapadye \ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ prapadye \ satyaṃ prapadye \\ ṛtaṃ prapadye \\ amṛtaṃ prapadye \ prajāpateḥ priyāṃ tanuvam anārtāṃ prapadye \ gāyatrīṃ prapadye \ triṣṭubhaṃ prapadye \ jagatīṃ prapadye \\ anuṣṭubhaṃ prapadye \ paṅktiṃ prapadye \ chandobhiś chādaye \ chanobhiś channo 'smi \\ idam ahaṃ pañcadaśena vajreṇa dviṣantaṃ bhrātṛvyam avakrāmāmi yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ /
21.0.1.c.d: भूः प्रपद्ये \ भुवः प्रपद्ये \ सुवः प्रपद्ये \ भूर् भुवः सुवः प्रपद्ये \ सत्यं प्रपद्ये \\ ऋतं प्रपद्ये \\ अमृतं प्रपद्ये \ प्रजापतेः प्रियां तनुवम् अनार्तां प्रपद्ये \ गायत्रीं प्रपद्ये \ त्रिष्टुभं प्रपद्ये \ जगतीं प्रपद्ये \\ अनुष्टुभं प्रपद्ये \ पङ्क्तिं प्रपद्ये \ छन्दोभिश् छादये \ छनोभिश् छन्नो ऽस्मि \\ इदम् अहं पञ्चदशेन वज्रेण द्विषन्तं भ्रातृव्यम् अवक्रामामि यो ऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मः ।
21.0.1.c.m: I resort to Bhūḥ; I resort to Bhuvaḥ; I resort to Suvaḥ; I resort to Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Suvaḥ; I resort to Truth; I resort to Cosmic Order; I resort to Immortality; I resort to the dear, uninjured body of Prajāpati; I resort to the Gāyatrī; I resort to the Triṣṭubh; I resort to the Jagatī; I resort to the Anuṣṭubh; I resort to the Paṅkti. With the meters I cover myself; by the meters am I covered. Here do I trample with the fifteenfold thunderbolt upon the hateful rival, who hates us and whom we hate.

21.0.1.f.m: We take hold from behind of Indra, appointed as domestic priest at the choosing of the hotṛ,

21.0.1.g.s: yenāyann uttamam̐ suvar devā aṅgiraso divam //
21.0.1.g.d: येनायन्न् उत्तमम्̐ सुवर् देवा अङ्गिरसो दिवम् ॥
21.0.1.g.m: by whom the gods, the Aṅgirases, went to the highest heaven, to the sky.

21.0.1.h.s: ṣaṣṭiś cādhvaryo navatiś ca pāśās \\ adhvaryum agnim antarā viyattāḥ / \ sinanti pākam ati dhīra eti \\ ṛtasya panthām anvemi hotā //
21.0.1.h.d: षष्टिश् चाध्वर्यो नवतिश् च पाशास् \\ अध्वर्युम् अग्निम् अन्तरा वियत्ताः । \ सिनन्ति पाकम् अति धीर एति \\ ऋतस्य पन्थाम् अन्वेमि होता ॥
21.0.1.h.m: Ninety and sixty fetters, O adhvaryu, / are stretched out between the adhvaryu and the fire; / they bind the foolish one; the wise one passes beyond them. / As hotṛ, I follow the path of Cosmic Order.

21.0.2.b.m: "May I not fall into the ocean; I follow the turning of the sun."

21.0.2.c.s: ṣaṇ morvīr am̐hasas pāntu dyauś ca pṛthivī cāhaś ca rātriś ca kṛṣiś ca vṛṣṭiś ca tviṣiś cāpacitiś cāpaś cauṣadhayaś ca /
21.0.2.c.d: षण् मोर्वीर् अम्̐हसस् पान्तु द्यौश् च पृथिवी चाहश् च रात्रिश् च कृषिश् च वृष्टिश् च त्विषिश् चापचितिश् चापश् चौषधयश् च ।
21.0.2.c.m: "May the six wide ones protect me from distress: heaven and earth, day and night, agriculture and rain, splendor and honour, waters and plants."

21.0.2.e.s: ye naḥ sapatnā apa te bhavantu \\ indrāgnibhyām avabādhāmahe tān / \ vasavo rudrā ādityā uparispṛśaṃ mā \\ ugraṃ cettāram adhirājam akran / j
21.0.2.e.d: ये नः सपत्ना अप ते भवन्तु \\ इन्द्राग्निभ्याम् अवबाधामहे तान् । \ वसवो रुद्रा आदित्या उपरिस्पृशं मा \\ उग्रं चेत्तारम् अधिराजम् अक्रन् । ज्
21.0.2.e.m: "Whatever rivals we have, let them be gone; / with Indra and Agni we thrust them away. / The Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas have made me touch what is above, / fierce, vigilant, supreme sovereign."

21.0.2.f.s: un nivata ud udvataś ca geṣam \\ pātaṃ mā dyāvāpṛthivī adyāhnaḥ /
21.0.2.f.d: उन् निवत उद् उद्वतश् च गेषम् \\ पातं मा द्यावापृथिवी अद्याह्नः ।
21.0.2.f.m: "May I go up from the lowlands and up the slopes; / protect me today, Heaven and Earth, from the day!"

21.0.2.g.s: sīda hotaḥ sva u loke cikitvān \ sādayo yajñam̐ sukṛtasya yonau / \ devāvīr devān haviṣā yajāsi \\ agne bṛhad yajamāne vayo dhāḥ /
21.0.2.g.d: सीद होतः स्व उ लोके चिकित्वान् \ सादयो यज्ञम्̐ सुकृतस्य योनौ । \ देवावीर् देवान् हविषा यजासि \\ अग्ने बृहद् यजमाने वयो धाः ।
21.0.2.g.m: "Sit, O hotṛ, in your own place, knowing; / settle the sacrifice in the womb of good deeds. / Welcoming the gods, worship the gods with the oblation; / O Agni, bestow great vigour upon the sacrificer!"

21.0.2.h.s: ni hotā hotṛṣadane vidānas \ tveṣo dīdivām̐ asadat sudakṣaḥ / \ adabdhavratapatir vasiṣṭhaḥ \ sahasraṃbharaḥ śucijihvo agniḥ //
21.0.2.h.d: नि होता होतृषदने विदानस् \ त्वेषो दीदिवाम्̐ असदत् सुदक्षः । \ अदब्धव्रतपतिर् वसिष्ठः \ सहस्रंभरः शुचिजिह्वो अग्निः ॥
21.0.2.h.m: The hotṛ has sat down in the seat of the hotṛ, knowing, / resplendent, shining, very clever, / the unbeguiled lord of rites, most excellent, / bearing thousands, pure-tongued Agni.

21.0.2.i.s: lokakṛtau lokaṃ me kṛṇutam \\ mā mā saṃtāptam \ eṣa vāṃ lokaḥ /
21.0.2.i.d: लोककृतौ लोकं मे कृणुतम् \\ मा मा संताप्तम् \ एष वां लोकः ।
21.0.2.i.m: "O two makers of space, make space for me; / do not scorch me; / this is your space."

21.0.2.j.s: pra me brūta bhāgadheyaṃ yathā vas \\ yena pathā havyamā vo vahāmi \ juṣṭām adya devebhyo vācam udyāsam \\ juṣṭāṃ brahmabhyas \\ juṣṭāṃ nārāśam̐sāya //
21.0.2.j.d: प्र मे ब्रूत भागधेयं यथा वस् \\ येन पथा हव्यमा वो वहामि \ जुष्टाम् अद्य देवेभ्यो वाचम् उद्यासम् \\ जुष्टां ब्रह्मभ्यस् \\ जुष्टां नाराशम्̐साय ॥
21.0.2.j.m: "Declare to me your share as [it is], / by which path I may bring the sacrificial oblation to you. / Today may I utter speech pleasing to the gods, / pleasing to the brahmans, / pleasing to Narāśaṃsa!"

21.0.2.k.s: vāg ojaḥ \ saha ojas \\ mayi prāṇāpānau / \ vāg vaṣaṭkāra namas te astu \ mā mā him̐sīḥ //
21.0.2.k.d: वाग् ओजः \ सह ओजस् \\ मयि प्राणापानौ । \ वाग् वषट्कार नमस् ते अस्तु \ मा मा हिम्̐सीः ॥
21.0.2.k.m: "Speech is power; / vigor is power; / in me are out-breath and in-breath. / O speech, O vaṣaṭ-call, homage be to you! / Do not harm me!"

21.1.1.a.m: We shall explain the hotṛ's duties in the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices.

21.1.2.a.s: kḷpte hotṛṣadane devā yo apsu mahimas \\ ity apa ācāmati //
21.1.2.a.d: कॢप्ते होतृषदने देवा यो अप्सु महिमस् \\ इत्य् अप आचामति ॥
21.1.2.a.m: When the seat of the hotṛ has been prepared, with [the mantra]: "O gods, whatever greatness is in the waters…", he sips water.

21.1.3.a.s: yajñopavītyācānto vihāram abhyetyāntareṇa vedyutkarau bhūḥ prapadye \ bhuvaḥ prapadye \\ iti pratipadyate / uttareṇa vedim avasthāya chandobhiś chādaye \ chandobhiś channo 'smi \\ iti japati //
21.1.3.a.d: यज्ञोपवीत्याचान्तो विहारम् अभ्येत्यान्तरेण वेद्युत्करौ भूः प्रपद्ये \ भुवः प्रपद्ये \\ इति प्रतिपद्यते । उत्तरेण वेदिम् अवस्थाय छन्दोभिश् छादये \ छन्दोभिश् छन्नो ऽस्मि \\ इति जपति ॥
21.1.3.a.m: Wearing the sacred cord over the left shoulder, having sipped water, he approaches the sacrificial area, and between the altar and the rubbish-heap he enters with [the mantras]: "I enter Bhūḥ;" "I enter Bhuvaḥ." Having stationed himself north of the altar, he mutters: "With the meters I cover [myself];" "I am covered with the meters."

21.1.4.a.s: dakṣiṇena pādenottarāṃ vediśroṇīm avakrāmati \\ idam ahaṃ pañcadaśena vajreṇa \\ iti //
21.1.4.a.d: दक्षिणेन पादेनोत्तरां वेदिश्रोणीम् अवक्रामति \\ इदम् अहं पञ्चदशेन वज्रेण \\ इति ॥
21.1.4.a.m: With his right foot he steps on the northern hip of the altar with: "Here I, with the fifteenfold thunderbolt…"

21.1.5.a.m: Standing there, he recites the kindling verses.

21.1.6.a.m: These [following] are the times when speech is to be restrained by one who is occupied:

21.1.7.a.s: sāmidhenīsaṃpraiṣādadhyā paridhānīyāyāḥ puronuvākyāsaṃpraiṣādadhyā praṇavādyājyāsaṃpraiṣādadhyā vaṣaṭkārān nigadam ārabhyāsamāpter hṛdayadeśe 'ñjaliṃ kṛtvānubrūyād yajec ca //
21.1.7.a.d: सामिधेनीसंप्रैषादध्या परिधानीयायाः पुरोनुवाक्यासंप्रैषादध्या प्रणवाद्याज्यासंप्रैषादध्या वषट्कारान् निगदम् आरभ्यासमाप्तेर् हृदयदेशे ऽञ्जलिं कृत्वानुब्रूयाद् यजेच् च ॥
21.1.7.a.m: From the direction for the kindling verses up to the concluding verse, from the direction for the introductory verse up to the praṇava, and from the direction for the offering verse up to the vaṣaṭ-call; having begun a formula, he should recite until its completion, making an añjali at the region of his heart, and he should offer.

21.1.8.a.s: athādhvaryuḥ saṃpreṣyati \\ agnaye samidhyamānāyānubrūhi \\ iti brahman sāmidhenīr anuvakṣyāmi \\ iti brahmāṇam āmantrayate / brahmann anuvakṣyāmi \\ iti vā / prasava ukte daśahotāraṃ vyākhyāya vyāhṛtīr japitvā him iti trir hiṃ karoti //
21.1.8.a.d: अथाध्वर्युः संप्रेष्यति \\ अग्नये समिध्यमानायानुब्रूहि \\ इति ब्रह्मन् सामिधेनीर् अनुवक्ष्यामि \\ इति ब्रह्माणम् आमन्त्रयते । ब्रह्मन्न् अनुवक्ष्यामि \\ इति वा । प्रसव उक्ते दशहोतारं व्याख्याय व्याहृतीर् जपित्वा हिम् इति त्रिर् हिं करोति ॥
21.1.8.a.m: Then the adhvaryu gives the ritual direction: "Recite for Agni being kindled!" He addresses the brahman priest: "O brahman, I shall recite the kindling verses;" or: "O brahman, I shall recite." When permission has been given, having explained the Daśahotṛ formula and muttered the sacred utterances, he utters hiṃ thrice with: "Hiṃ!"

21.1.9.a.s: pra vo vājā abhidyavas \\ iti pañcadaśa sāmidhenīr anvāha madhyamasvareṇeti vijñāyate //
21.1.9.a.d: प्र वो वाजा अभिद्यवस् \\ इति पञ्चदश सामिधेनीर् अन्वाह मध्यमस्वरेणेति विज्ञायते ॥
21.1.9.a.m: He recites the fifteen kindling verses beginning with: "Forward your prizes, heavenly…" in the middle pitch—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

21.1.10.a.s: yat krauñcam anvāhāsuraṃ tad yan mandraṃ mānuṣaṃ tad yad antarā tat sadevam antarānūcyam̐ sadevatvāya //
21.1.10.a.d: यत् क्रौञ्चम् अन्वाहासुरं तद् यन् मन्द्रं मानुषं तद् यद् अन्तरा तत् सदेवम् अन्तरानूच्यम्̐ सदेवत्वाय ॥
21.1.10.a.m: What he recites in the curlew tone is asuric; what is low is human; what is between, that belongs to the gods; it should be recited between [them] for the sake of divinity.

21.1.11.a.s: triḥ prathamām anvāha trir uttamām anavānaṃ tā evaṃ pañcadaś asaṃpadyante //
21.1.11.a.d: त्रिः प्रथमाम् अन्वाह त्रिर् उत्तमाम् अनवानं ता एवं पञ्चदश् असंपद्यन्ते ॥
21.1.11.a.m: He recites the first [verse] three times, and the last three times, without taking breath; thus they amount to fifteen.

21.1.12.a.s: api vānuvacane'nuvacane 'pānity uttame 'nuvacane \\ agna āyāhi vītaye \\ ity etasyā ardharce 'pānity evam itarāsu pūrvasyāś cottaram uttarasyāś ca pūrvam ardharcau saṃdadhāti //
21.1.12.a.d: अपि वानुवचनेऽनुवचने ऽपानित्य् उत्तमे ऽनुवचने \\ अग्न आयाहि वीतये \\ इत्य् एतस्या अर्धर्चे ऽपानित्य् एवम् इतरासु पूर्वस्याश् चोत्तरम् उत्तरस्याश् च पूर्वम् अर्धर्चौ संदधाति ॥
21.1.12.a.m: Alternatively, at each recitation he inhales; at the final recitation he inhales at the half-verse of this [verse]: "O Agni, come to the feast…"; likewise in the others he joins the latter half-verse of the preceding [verse] and the former half-verse of the following [verse].

21.1.13.a.m: At the end of all the verses he places the praṇava.

21.1.14.a.s: oṃkāram udāttam ṛcā sam̐hitam ūnam athavā pūrṇam om ity ūnam o3m iti pūrṇaṃ pūrṇam evāvasānīyaṃ yad ṛcy uttamaṃ chandomānaṃ tad apohya tasya sthāne yat pūrṇaṃ chandomānaṃ tasya vyañjanaṃ na tal lupyate //
21.1.14.a.d: ओंकारम् उदात्तम् ऋचा सम्̐हितम् ऊनम् अथवा पूर्णम् ओम् इत्य् ऊनम् ओ3म् इति पूर्णं पूर्णम् एवावसानीयं यद् ऋच्य् उत्तमं छन्दोमानं तद् अपोह्य तस्य स्थाने यत् पूर्णं छन्दोमानं तस्य व्यञ्जनं न तल् लुप्यते ॥
21.1.14.a.m: The syllable Om is high-pitched, joined with the verse, [either] deficient or full: "Om" is deficient, "O3m" is full; the final one must indeed be full; setting aside the last metrical measure in the verse, in its place is that which is the full metrical measure; its consonant is not dropped.

21.1.15.a.s: taṃ tvā samidbhir aṅgiras \\ ity etām̐ sāmidhenīṃ trir vigṛhṇāti / samiddho agne \\ iti //
21.1.15.a.d: तं त्वा समिद्भिर् अङ्गिरस् \\ इत्य् एताम्̐ सामिधेनीं त्रिर् विगृह्णाति । समिद्धो अग्ने \\ इति ॥
21.1.15.a.m: This kindling verse: "Thee with fuel, O Aṅgiras…", he divides three times: "O Agni, kindled…"

21.1.16.a.s: so 'vadhyāyikaṃ padaṃ pratiṣidya dadhāti / tathā srugādāpana uttamaṃ nasyām āha \\ upahūteḍā \\ upahūteḍā \\ itīḍāyām / śaṃ no astu dvipade śaṃ catuṣpat \\ iti śaṃyuvāke / yac cānyat prakṛtāv evaṃjātīyam̐ syāt tad eva tatra niyamyeta //
21.1.16.a.d: सो ऽवध्यायिकं पदं प्रतिषिद्य दधाति । तथा स्रुगादापन उत्तमं नस्याम् आह \\ उपहूतेडा \\ उपहूतेडा \\ इतीडायाम् । शं नो अस्तु द्विपदे शं चतुष्पत् \\ इति शंयुवाके । यच् चान्यत् प्रकृताव् एवंजातीयम्̐ स्यात् तद् एव तत्र नियम्येत ॥
21.1.16.a.m: Setting aside the [extraneous] word relating to Vedic study, he inserts [the verse]. Likewise, when handing over the ladles, he speaks the last [word] in his nose: "Iḍā is invoked, / iḍā is invoked," at the iḍā; "May there be peace for our two-footed, peace for the four-footed," in the Śaṃyuvāka; and whatever else of this kind should occur in the archetypal rite, that alone should be restricted there.

21.1.17.a.m: He concludes with the next [verse]: "Offer! Serve!"

21.1.18.a.m: [With the verse:] "Thou art Varuṇa…" for Vasiṣṭhas and Rājanyas.

21.1.19.b.s: yadi kāmayeta brahmavarcasam astv iti gāyatriyā paridadhyāt //
21.1.19.b.d: यदि कामयेत ब्रह्मवर्चसम् अस्त्व् इति गायत्रिया परिदध्यात् ॥
21.1.19.b.m: If he should desire: 'Let there be spiritual luster,' he should conclude with a gāyatrī [verse].

21.2.1.a.s: trīm̐s tṛcān anubrūyād brāhmaṇasya / trīm̐s tṛcān anubrūyād rājanyasya / trīm̐s tṛcān anubrūyād vaiśyasyeti vijñāyate //
21.2.1.a.d: त्रीम्̐स् तृचान् अनुब्रूयाद् ब्राह्मणस्य । त्रीम्̐स् तृचान् अनुब्रूयाद् राजन्यस्य । त्रीम्̐स् तृचान् अनुब्रूयाद् वैश्यस्येति विज्ञायते ॥
21.2.1.a.m: He should recite three triplets for a brāhmaṇa; he should recite three triplets for a rājanya; he should recite three triplets for a vaiśya—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

21.2.2.a.m: They should alternate with the fifteenfold [recitation].

21.2.3.a.s: vaiśyasya sāptadaśyena / tasya pṛṭhupājavatyau dhāyye purastāt samiddhavatyāḥ //
21.2.3.a.d: वैश्यस्य साप्तदश्येन । तस्य पृठुपाजवत्यौ धाय्ये पुरस्तात् समिद्धवत्याः ॥
21.2.3.a.m: With the seventeenfold [recitation] for a Vaiśya; for him, the two verses containing the word pṛthupājas are the two inserted verses before the one containing the word samiddha.

21.2.4.a.s: ekavim̐śatim anubrūyād iti brāhmaṇavyākhyātāḥ kāmyāḥ sāmidhenīkalpās teṣāṃ pāñcadaśyena dharmā vyākhyātāḥ //
21.2.4.a.d: एकविम्̐शतिम् अनुब्रूयाद् इति ब्राह्मणव्याख्याताः काम्याः सामिधेनीकल्पास् तेषां पाञ्चदश्येन धर्मा व्याख्याताः ॥
21.2.4.a.m: 'He should recite twenty-one'—thus are the optional procedures for the kindling verses explained by the Brāhmaṇa; their rules are explained by the fifteenfold [model].

21.2.5.a.s: bahuyājina iti gāyatrītriṣṭubjagatīṣu sarvartusomayājī bahuyājī bhavatīti vijñāyate //
21.2.5.a.d: बहुयाजिन इति गायत्रीत्रिष्टुब्जगतीषु सर्वर्तुसोमयाजी बहुयाजी भवतीति विज्ञायते ॥
21.2.5.a.m: [The Brāhmaṇa says:] 'for one who has sacrificed much', among gāyatrī, triṣṭubh, and jagatī verses; one who has sacrificed with soma in all seasons becomes 'one who has sacrificed much'—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

21.2.6.a.s: aparimitam anubrūyād iti / ūrdhvam aṣṭācatvārim̐śataṃ parimāṇeṣu yāthākāmyante 'dhīyīran / yāsāṃ tu vikṛtau dhāyyāśabdena vidhānaṃ bhavati yathāpṛthupājavatyau dhāyye / anumatyau dhāyye / uṣṇikkakubhau dhāyye / mānavī ṛcau dhāyye kuryād iti purastāt samiddhavatyā āgamayed gāyatrīr āgneyīr āgamayet tathāgamayed yathā prathamottamayor āvṛttyā saṃkhyā pūryeta //
21.2.6.a.d: अपरिमितम् अनुब्रूयाद् इति । ऊर्ध्वम् अष्टाचत्वारिम्̐शतं परिमाणेषु याथाकाम्यन्ते ऽधीयीरन् । यासां तु विकृतौ धाय्याशब्देन विधानं भवति यथापृथुपाजवत्यौ धाय्ये । अनुमत्यौ धाय्ये । उष्णिक्ककुभौ धाय्ये । मानवी ऋचौ धाय्ये कुर्याद् इति पुरस्तात् समिद्धवत्या आगमयेद् गायत्रीर् आग्नेयीर् आगमयेत् तथागमयेद् यथा प्रथमोत्तमयोर् आवृत्त्या संख्या पूर्येत ॥
21.2.6.a.m: [The Brāhmaṇa says:] 'He should recite without limit.' Above forty-eight, among the measures, they may study as they wish; but those which in a modified rite are prescribed under the name of 'dhāyyā', such as 'the two dhāyyās containing pṛthupājas', 'the two dhāyyās to Anumati', 'the two dhāyyās in uṣṇih and kakubh', 'he should make two verses of Manu the dhāyyās'—he should bring them in before the verse containing samiddha, bringing in gāyatrī verses addressed to Agni; he should bring them in such that the count is completed by the repetition of the first and the last verses.

21.2.7.a.s: uttame 'nuvacane \\ agne mahām̐ asi brāhmaṇa bhārata \\ ity atrāpāniti //
21.2.7.a.d: उत्तमे ऽनुवचने \\ अग्ने महाम्̐ असि ब्राह्मण भारत \\ इत्य् अत्रापानिति ॥
21.2.7.a.m: At the last recitation: "O Agni, thou art great, O brāhmaṇa, descendant of Bharata…", here he inhales.

21.2.8.a.s: atha pravaraṃ pravṛṇite / yathā yajamānasyārṣeyam̐ saha pareṇa trīnanantarānamuto 'rvāca ityāmantraṇena bhārgavavāsiṣṭheti vijñāyate //
21.2.8.a.d: अथ प्रवरं प्रवृणिते । यथा यजमानस्यार्षेयम्̐ सह परेण त्रीननन्तरानमुतो ऽर्वाच इत्यामन्त्रणेन भार्गववासिष्ठेति विज्ञायते ॥
21.2.8.a.m: Then he recites the ancestral invocation: according to the ancestral rishi-lineage of the sacrificer, together with the higher one, three immediately successive [ancestors] from that end downwards, with the vocative address: "O descendant of Bhṛgu, O descendant of Vasiṣṭha!"—so it is known.

21.2.9.a.s: ekaṃ vṛṇīte dvau vṛṇīte trīn vṛṇīte na caturo vṛṇīte na pañcāni pravṛṇīta iti kṛtsnasya pravarasya sthāne mānava \\ ity eva brūyād ity ekeṣām //
21.2.9.a.d: एकं वृणीते द्वौ वृणीते त्रीन् वृणीते न चतुरो वृणीते न पञ्चानि प्रवृणीत इति कृत्स्नस्य प्रवरस्य स्थाने मानव \\ इत्य् एव ब्रूयाद् इत्य् एकेषाम् ॥
21.2.9.a.m: 'He chooses one, he chooses two, he chooses three; he does not choose four; he does not choose five.' In place of the entire ancestral invocation he should simply say: "O descendant of Manu!"—thus say some.

21.2.10.a.s: atha nivido dadhāti // deveddho manviddhas \\ iti pratipadyate / sapta padāny uktvāpāniti //
21.2.10.a.d: अथ निविदो दधाति ॥ देवेद्धो मन्विद्धस् \\ इति प्रतिपद्यते । सप्त पदान्य् उक्त्वापानिति ॥
21.2.10.a.m: Then he introduces the nivid formulas. He begins with: "Kindled by the gods, kindled by Manu…" Having spoken seven words, he inhales.

21.2.12.a.s: devatā āvāhayati \\ agnim agna āvaha \ somam āvaha \\ agnim āvaha \ prajāpatim āvaha \\ agnīṣomāv āvaha \\ ity agnīṣomīye puroḍāśa iti paurṇamāsyām //
21.2.12.a.d: देवता आवाहयति \\ अग्निम् अग्न आवह \ सोमम् आवह \\ अग्निम् आवह \ प्रजापतिम् आवह \\ अग्नीषोमाव् आवह \\ इत्य् अग्नीषोमीये पुरोडाश इति पौर्णमास्याम् ॥
21.2.12.a.m: He summons the deities: "O Agni, bring Agni hither! Bring Soma hither! Bring Agni hither! Bring Prajāpati hither! Bring Agni and Soma hither!" for the sacrificial cake dedicated to Agni and Soma, at the Full Moon rite.

21.2.13.a.m: At the New Moon rite, the inaudible offering does not exist.

21.2.14.a.s: ūrdhvam āgneyasyāvāhanāt \\ indrāgnī āvaha \\ ity asaṃnayatas \\ indram āvaha \\ iti saṃnayata indrayājinas \\ mahendram āvaha \\ iti mahendrayājinas \\ devām̐ ājyapām̐ āvaha \\ iti samānam ubhayatra //
21.2.14.a.d: ऊर्ध्वम् आग्नेयस्यावाहनात् \\ इन्द्राग्नी आवह \\ इत्य् असंनयतस् \\ इन्द्रम् आवह \\ इति संनयत इन्द्रयाजिनस् \\ महेन्द्रम् आवह \\ इति महेन्द्रयाजिनस् \\ देवाम्̐ आज्यपाम्̐ आवह \\ इति समानम् उभयत्र ॥
21.2.14.a.m: After the invocation of Agni: "Bring Indra and Agni" for one who does not perform the saṃnāyya; "Bring Indra" for one who performs the saṃnāyya and sacrifices to Indra; "Bring Mahendra" for one who sacrifices to Mahendra; "Bring the gods who drink clarified butter" is common in both cases.

21.2.15.a.m: Facing the election, he sits down with his right knee raised.

21.2.16.a.s: ūrdhvajñur āsīno vṛṇīta iti hetur vijñāyate //
21.2.16.a.d: ऊर्ध्वज्ञुर् आसीनो वृणीत इति हेतुर् विज्ञायते ॥
21.2.16.a.m: "Sitting with his right knee raised, he should choose [the hotṛ]," thus the Brāhmaṇa passage is known.

21.2.17.a.s: yatrābhijānāti \\ asau mānuṣas \\ iti tad upotthāya namo mātre pṛthivyai \\ iti pṛthivīm abhimṛśati //
21.2.17.a.d: यत्राभिजानाति \\ असौ मानुषस् \\ इति तद् उपोत्थाय नमो मात्रे पृथिव्यै \\ इति पृथिवीम् अभिमृशति ॥
21.2.17.a.m: When he recognizes: "Such-and-such mortal," then rising up toward it he touches the earth with: "Homage to Mother Earth."

21.2.18.a.s: caturhotrāraṃ pañcahotāram̐ ṣaḍḍhotāram̐ saptahotāram iti japitvā \\ indram anvārabhāmahe \\ iti dakṣiṇena hastenādhvaryum anvārabhate //
21.2.18.a.d: चतुर्होत्रारं पञ्चहोतारम्̐ षड्ढोतारम्̐ सप्तहोतारम् इति जपित्वा \\ इन्द्रम् अन्वारभामहे \\ इति दक्षिणेन हस्तेनाध्वर्युम् अन्वारभते ॥
21.2.18.a.m: Having whispered the Caturhotṛ, Pañcahotṛ, Ṣaḍḍhotṛ, and Saptahotṛ formulas, he touches the adhvaryu with his right hand, saying: "We take hold of Indra."

21.2.19.a.m: Silently [he touches] the āgnīdhra with his left [hand].

21.2.20.a.s: ṣaṣṭiś cādhvaryo navatiś ca pāśās \\ ity antareṇāhavanīyam adhvaryuṃ ca pratyaṅṅ etya samudraṃ māvapadam ādityasyāvṛtam anvāvarte \\ iti pradakṣiṇam anvāvartate //
21.2.20.a.d: षष्टिश् चाध्वर्यो नवतिश् च पाशास् \\ इत्य् अन्तरेणाहवनीयम् अध्वर्युं च प्रत्यङ्ङ् एत्य समुद्रं मावपदम् आदित्यस्यावृतम् अन्वावर्ते \\ इति प्रदक्षिणम् अन्वावर्तते ॥
21.2.20.a.m: With: "Sixty, O adhvaryu, and ninety are the snares," going westward between the āhavanīya and the adhvaryu, he turns around clockwise with: "Lest I step down into the ocean, I turn following the course of the sun."

21.2.21.a.s: ṣaṇ morvīr am̐hasas pāntu tvā \\ iti japitvā hotṛṣadanaṃ prāpya nirastaḥ parāvasur iti hotṛṣadanāt tṛṇaṃ nirasyāpa upaspṛśya ye naḥ sapatnā apa te bhavantu \\ iti hotṛṣadanam avabādhate 'bhyukṣya hotṛṣadanam un nivata ud udvataś ca geṣam iti / upaviśati sīda hotar iti ca //
21.2.21.a.d: षण् मोर्वीर् अम्̐हसस् पान्तु त्वा \\ इति जपित्वा होतृषदनं प्राप्य निरस्तः परावसुर् इति होतृषदनात् तृणं निरस्याप उपस्पृश्य ये नः सपत्ना अप ते भवन्तु \\ इति होतृषदनम् अवबाधते ऽभ्युक्ष्य होतृषदनम् उन् निवत उद् उद्वतश् च गेषम् इति । उपविशति सीद होतर् इति च ॥
21.2.21.a.m: Having whispered: "May the six wide ones protect you from distress," reaching the seat of the hotṛ, casting away a blade of grass from the seat of the hotṛ with: "Cast away is Parāvasu," touching water, he presses down upon the seat of the hotṛ with: "Those who are our rivals, let them be driven away;" having sprinkled the seat of the hotṛ, with: "May I pass up from the depths and up from the heights," he sits down, and with: "Sit down, O hotṛ."

21.2.22.a.s: ni hotā hotṛṣadane \\ ity āsīno japati //
21.2.22.a.d: नि होता होतृषदने \\ इत्य् आसीनो जपति ॥
21.2.22.a.m: Sitting, he whispers: "The hotṛ has sat down in the seat of the hotṛ."

21.2.23.a.s: lokakṛtau lokaṃ me kṛṇutam iti gārhapatyāhavanīyau samīkṣate //
21.2.23.a.d: लोककृतौ लोकं मे कृणुतम् इति गार्हपत्याहवनीयौ समीक्षते ॥
21.2.23.a.m: He looks at the gārhapatya and āhavanīya fires with: "O world-makers, make a world for me."

21.2.24.a.s: pra me brūta bhāgadheyam iti devatā upatiṣṭhate //
21.2.24.a.d: प्र मे ब्रूत भागधेयम् इति देवता उपतिष्ठते ॥
21.2.24.a.m: He reverences the deities with: "Declare to me my share."

21.2.25.a.s: tataḥ srucāv ādāpayati \\ agnir hotā vettv agnir hotraṃ vettu \\ iti //
21.2.25.a.d: ततः स्रुचाव् आदापयति \\ अग्निर् होता वेत्त्व् अग्निर् होत्रं वेत्तु \\ इति ॥
21.2.25.a.m: Then he causes the [adhvaryu] to take up the two ladles with: "May Agni the hotṛ know; may Agni know the hotṛ's office."

21.2.26.a.s: mandreṇa sthānena prāg ājyabhāgābhyām / madhyamena pradhānāni / uttamena sviṣṭakṛtprabhṛti //
21.2.26.a.d: मन्द्रेण स्थानेन प्राग् आज्यभागाभ्याम् । मध्यमेन प्रधानानि । उत्तमेन स्विष्टकृत्प्रभृति ॥
21.2.26.a.m: With a low voice before the two clarified butter portions; with a middle voice for the primary rites; with a high voice beginning with the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

21.2.27.a.s: samidho yaja \\ iti saṃpreṣite samidho agna ājyasya viyantu \\ iti yajati / tanūnapād agna ājyasya vettu \\ iti dvitīyam / narāśam̐so dvitīyaḥ prayājo vasiṣṭhaśunakānāṃ narāśam̐so agna ājyasya vettu \\ iti \\ iḍo agna ājyasya viyantu \\ iti tṛtīyam / barhir agna ājyasya vettu \\ iti caturtham \\ svāhāgnim \\ svāhā somam \\ svāhāmum iti cottame prayāje yathoktadevatā upalakṣayati //
21.2.27.a.d: समिधो यज \\ इति संप्रेषिते समिधो अग्न आज्यस्य वियन्तु \\ इति यजति । तनूनपाद् अग्न आज्यस्य वेत्तु \\ इति द्वितीयम् । नराशम्̐सो द्वितीयः प्रयाजो वसिष्ठशुनकानां नराशम्̐सो अग्न आज्यस्य वेत्तु \\ इति \\ इडो अग्न आज्यस्य वियन्तु \\ इति तृतीयम् । बर्हिर् अग्न आज्यस्य वेत्तु \\ इति चतुर्थम् \\ स्वाहाग्निम् \\ स्वाहा सोमम् \\ स्वाहामुम् इति चोत्तमे प्रयाजे यथोक्तदेवता उपलक्षयति ॥
21.2.27.a.m: When directed with: "Sacrifice to the Samidhs," he recites the offering verse: "May the Samidhs, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter;" "May Tanūnapāt, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter" is the second; for the Vasiṣṭhas and Śunakas the second fore-offering is Narāśaṃsa: "May Narāśaṃsa, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter;" "May the Iḍs, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter" is the third; "May the Barhis, O Agni, partake of the clarified butter" is the fourth; and in the final fore-offering he names the deities as prescribed with: "Svāhā to Agni," "Svāhā to Soma," "Svāhā to such-and-such."

21.2.28.a.m: Then he proceeds with the two clarified butter portions.

21.2.29.a.m: For these two there are offering verses and introductory verses.

21.2.30.a.m: For the fore-offerings and after-offerings, there are only offering verses.

21.2.31.a.s: teṣāṃ pracarya sarvāsu puronuvākyāsu praṇavaṃ dadhāti sa vyākhyātaḥ //
21.2.31.a.d: तेषां प्रचर्य सर्वासु पुरोनुवाक्यासु प्रणवं दधाति स व्याख्यातः ॥
21.2.31.a.m: Having performed these, he applies the praṇava to all the introductory verses; that has been explained.

21.2.32.a.s: atha yājyāyā yad ṛcy uttamaṃ chandomānaṃ tenodāttenābhisaṃdadhat \\ vauṣaṭ \\ iti vaṣaṭkaroti //
21.2.32.a.d: अथ याज्याया यद् ऋच्य् उत्तमं छन्दोमानं तेनोदात्तेनाभिसंदधत् \\ वौषट् \\ इति वषट्करोति ॥
21.2.32.a.m: Then, connecting with the highest metrical unit in the verse of the offering verse using the acute accent, he pronounces the vaṣaṭ with: "Vauṣaṭ."

21.2.33.a.s: tatraitad ekāraikārau yājyānte bhavataḥ / āikāraṃ tatra kuryād yatraukāraukārāv āukāraṃ tatra kuryāt / ity atra pragrahebhyo 'tha yatra kavargaprathamā yājyānte syus tṛtīyam̐ svavargīyaṃ makāre paravanna ṅakāraṇakāranakāreṣu vikāraḥ //
21.2.33.a.d: तत्रैतद् एकारैकारौ याज्यान्ते भवतः । आइकारं तत्र कुर्याद् यत्रौकारौकाराव् आउकारं तत्र कुर्यात् । इत्य् अत्र प्रग्रहेभ्यो ऽथ यत्र कवर्गप्रथमा याज्यान्ते स्युस् तृतीयम्̐ स्ववर्गीयं मकारे परवन्न ङकारणकारनकारेषु विकारः ॥
21.2.33.a.m: Here, these two sounds, e and ai, occur at the end of an offering verse; there one should make āi; where there are o and au, there one should make āu; thus in these cases before pause vowels. Then where the first consonants of the guttural class are at the end of an offering verse, the third consonant of its own class [is substituted] when followed by m, [and] there is no alteration before ṅ, ṇ, and n.

21.2.34.a.s: atha yatrāvarṇopadho visarjanīyaḥ / ākāraṃ dīrghaṃ rathate 'nusarepham ivarṇopadha īkāram uvarṇopadha ūkāraṃ vaṣaṭkāro yājyāntāḥ plutāḥ svarāvyañjanāntāyāḥ pūrvo brūhi praiṣyoṃkārau śrauṣaṭ \\ ity avasāne vīhi \\ iti ca vaha ā ca vaha ye yajāmahe paraṃ ca / na svaṃ mahimānam āvaha \\ iti \\ āśrāvayośrāvaya ghorā ye iti vibhāṣā, īdṛgayaṇety ubhayataḥ plāvanaṃ vyākāraṇam / sarvatra na plāvayen na ca śrūyata iti kāśakṛtsnasya //
21.2.34.a.d: अथ यत्रावर्णोपधो विसर्जनीयः । आकारं दीर्घं रथते ऽनुसरेफम् इवर्णोपध ईकारम् उवर्णोपध ऊकारं वषट्कारो याज्यान्ताः प्लुताः स्वराव्यञ्जनान्तायाः पूर्वो ब्रूहि प्रैष्योंकारौ श्रौषट् \\ इत्य् अवसाने वीहि \\ इति च वह आ च वह ये यजामहे परं च । न स्वं महिमानम् आवह \\ इति \\ आश्रावयोश्रावय घोरा ये इति विभाषा, ईदृगयणेत्य् उभयतः प्लावनं व्याकारणम् । सर्वत्र न प्लावयेन् न च श्रूयत इति काशकृत्स्नस्य ॥
21.2.34.a.m: Then where a visarga has a preceding a-vowel, it becomes an elongated ā followed by an r; if preceded by an i-vowel, an ī; if preceded by an u-vowel, an ū. The vaṣaṭ-call, the ends of offering verses, and the vowels preceding a final consonant are protracted; also the word "brūhi" in directions, the oṃkāra, "śrauṣaṭ", and at the pause "vīhi", and "vaha", "ā ca vaha", and "ye yajāmahe", and what follows; not in "svaṃ mahimānam āvaha"; "āśrāvaya", "ośrāvaya", "ghorā ye" are optional; prolongation on both sides is an exceptional rule according to Īdṛgayana; according to Kāśakṛtsna, one should not prolong anywhere, nor is it taught in the Veda.

21.2.35.a.s: cekitāno yathālakṣaṇaṃ tu pravacanaśeṣo 'bhilakṣaṇaṃ brūhi \\ iti puronuvākyāsaṃpraiṣas \\ yaja \\ iti yājyāsaṃpraiṣas \\ ye yajāmahe \\ iti prativacanaḥ //
21.2.35.a.d: चेकितानो यथालक्षणं तु प्रवचनशेषो ऽभिलक्षणं ब्रूहि \\ इति पुरोनुवाक्यासंप्रैषस् \\ यज \\ इति याज्यासंप्रैषस् \\ ये यजामहे \\ इति प्रतिवचनः ॥
21.2.35.a.m: The rest of the oral instruction follows the rule for one who understands: "brūhi" is the direction for an introductory verse; "yaja" is the direction for an offering verse; "ye yajāmahe" is the response.

21.2.36.a.s: ye yajāmahe 'mum iti yathādevatam upalakṣya vyāhṛtīr japitvā yājyānte vaṣaṭkaroti //
21.2.36.a.d: ये यजामहे ऽमुम् इति यथादेवतम् उपलक्ष्य व्याहृतीर् जपित्वा याज्यान्ते वषट्करोति ॥
21.2.36.a.m: Having designated according to the deity: "We who sacrifice to such-and-such," having whispered the vyāhṛtis, he utters the vaṣaṭ-call at the end of the offering verse.

21.2.37.a.s: vaṣaṭ \\ ity eke samāmananti / vauṣaṭ \\ ity eke / vāṣaṭ \\ ity eke / vaṣāṭ \\ ity eke //
21.2.37.a.d: वषट् \\ इत्य् एके समामनन्ति । वौषट् \\ इत्य् एके । वाषट् \\ इत्य् एके । वषाट् \\ इत्य् एके ॥

21.2.38.a.m: "He utters the vaṣaṭ-call continuously with the verse," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

21.2.39.a.m: "He utters the vaṣaṭ-call more strongly than the verse," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

21.2.40.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta pāpīyānt syād iti nīcaistarāṃ tasya yājyāyā vaṣaṭkuryāt //
21.2.40.a.d: यं कामयेत पापीयान्त् स्याद् इति नीचैस्तरां तस्य याज्याया वषट्कुर्यात् ॥
21.2.40.a.m: For whomever he might wish that he become worse off, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call of his offering verse lower.

21.2.41.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta na pāpīyān na kṣeyān iti samaṃ tasya yājyāyā vaṣaṭkuryāt //
21.2.41.a.d: यं कामयेत न पापीयान् न क्षेयान् इति समं तस्य याज्याया वषट्कुर्यात् ॥
21.2.41.a.m: For whomever he might wish that he become neither worse off nor better off, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call of his offering verse at an equal level.

21.2.42.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta vasīyāñ chreyānt syād ity uccaistarāṃ tasya yājyāyā vaṣaṭkuryāt //
21.2.42.a.d: यं कामयेत वसीयाञ् छ्रेयान्त् स्याद् इत्य् उच्चैस्तरां तस्य याज्याया वषट्कुर्यात् ॥
21.2.42.a.m: For whomever he might wish that he become wealthier and better off, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call of his offering verse higher.

21.2.43.a.s: apagūrya vaṣaṭkaroti stṛtyā ity uccair vā śabdasaṃyogāt //
21.2.43.a.d: अपगूर्य वषट्करोति स्तृत्या इत्य् उच्चैर् वा शब्दसंयोगात् ॥
21.2.43.a.m: He utters the vaṣaṭ-call loudly with a threatening tone, for vanquishing, due to connection with sound.

21.2.44.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta pramāyukaḥ syād iti tasyoccair apagūrya niṣkhidanti vaṣaṭkuryād ity uccaiḥ krauñcam iva vaṣaṭkuryāt svargakāmasyeti vijñāyate //
21.2.44.a.d: यं कामयेत प्रमायुकः स्याद् इति तस्योच्चैर् अपगूर्य निष्खिदन्ति वषट्कुर्याद् इत्य् उच्चैः क्रौञ्चम् इव वषट्कुर्यात् स्वर्गकामस्येति विज्ञायते ॥
21.2.44.a.m: "For whomever he might wish that he perish, having threatened loudly, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call dragging it down; loudly like a crane he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call for one desiring heaven," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

21.2.45.a.s: vaṣaṭkṛtyavaṣaṭkṛtya prāṇyāpānya nimiṣet / vāg ojaḥ \ saha ojas \\ vāg vaṣaṭkāro namas te astu \ mā mā him̐sīr iti prayuktaṃ vaṣaṭkāram anumantrayate //
21.2.45.a.d: वषट्कृत्यवषट्कृत्य प्राण्यापान्य निमिषेत् । वाग् ओजः \ सह ओजस् \\ वाग् वषट्कारो नमस् ते अस्तु \ मा मा हिम्̐सीर् इति प्रयुक्तं वषट्कारम् अनुमन्त्रयते ॥
21.2.45.a.m: Having uttered each vaṣaṭ-call, having breathed in and breathed out, he should blink; he accompanies the employed vaṣaṭ-call with the mantra: "Speech is vigor, might is vigor; O Speech, O vaṣaṭ-call, homage be to you; do not harm me."

21.2.46.a.s: agnir vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanat \\ ity āgneyasyājyabhāgasya puronuvākyā / tvam̐ somāsi satpatir iti somasya vṛdhanvatī / amāvāsyāyām agniḥ pratnena janmanā \\ ity āgneyasya / soma gīrbhiṣ ṭvā vayam iti saumyasya / samānī yājye ājyabhāgau juṣāṇā yājyāv eke samāmananti // ṛgyājyāv eke / samāviṣāv eke / amūham ity uttaram āheti vijñāyate //
21.2.46.a.d: अग्निर् वृत्राणि जङ्घनत् \\ इत्य् आग्नेयस्याज्यभागस्य पुरोनुवाक्या । त्वम्̐ सोमासि सत्पतिर् इति सोमस्य वृधन्वती । अमावास्यायाम् अग्निः प्रत्नेन जन्मना \\ इत्य् आग्नेयस्य । सोम गीर्भिष् ट्वा वयम् इति सौम्यस्य । समानी याज्ये आज्यभागौ जुषाणा याज्याव् एके समामनन्ति ॥ ऋग्याज्याव् एके । समाविषाव् एके । अमूहम् इत्य् उत्तरम् आहेति विज्ञायते ॥
21.2.46.a.m: "Agni shall slay the Vṛtras" is the introductory verse for the clarified butter portion to Agni; "You, O Soma, are the true protector" containing the word vṛdh is for Soma; on the New Moon rite: "Agni with his ancient birth" is for Agni; "O Soma, we with our songs to you" is for Soma; the two offering verses are identical; some recite the formulas beginning with "juṣāṇā" as the two offering verses; some, two verses as offering verses; some, two containing "samāviṣṭau"; "he speaks the latter with amūham," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

21.2.47.a.s: atha pradhānānāṃ yājyānuvākyā agnir mūrdhā \ bhuva ity āgneyasya prajāpate savedasā \\ ity upām̐śuyājasya //
21.2.47.a.d: अथ प्रधानानां याज्यानुवाक्या अग्निर् मूर्धा \ भुव इत्य् आग्नेयस्य प्रजापते सवेदसा \\ इत्य् उपाम्̐शुयाजस्य ॥
21.2.47.a.m: Now the offering verses and introductory verses of the primary rites: "Agni is the head...", "You became..." for that to Agni; "O Prajāpati, together with wealth..." for the inaudible offering;

21.2.48.a.s: agnīṣomā \ yuvam ity agnīṣomīyasyendrāgnī rocanād iva śnathad vṛtram ity aindrāgnasya \\ endra sānasim̐ rayim \\ prasasāhiṣe \\ ity aindrasya mahām̐ indro ya ojasā \ mahām̐ indro nṛvat \\ iti māhendrasya //
21.2.48.a.d: अग्नीषोमा \ युवम् इत्य् अग्नीषोमीयस्येन्द्राग्नी रोचनाद् इव श्नथद् वृत्रम् इत्य् ऐन्द्राग्नस्य \\ एन्द्र सानसिम्̐ रयिम् \\ प्रससाहिषे \\ इत्य् ऐन्द्रस्य महाम्̐ इन्द्रो य ओजसा \ महाम्̐ इन्द्रो नृवत् \\ इति माहेन्द्रस्य ॥
21.2.48.a.m: "O Agni and Soma...", "You two..." for that to Agni and Soma; "O Indra and Agni, from the realm of light...", "He struck down Vṛtra..." for that to Indra and Agni; "Come here, O Indra, with winning wealth...", "You have overpowered..." for that to Indra; "Great is Indra who with might...", "Great is Indra, manly..." for that to Mahendra;

21.2.49.a.s: piprīhi devām̐ uśato yaviṣṭha iti sviṣṭakṛtaḥ puronuvākyā ye yajāmahe \\ agnim̐ sviṣṭakṛtam \ āyāḍ amuṣya \\ ayāḍ amuṣya \\ iti yathoktadevatā upalakṣya \\ agne yad adya viśo adhvarasya hotar iti yajati //
21.2.49.a.d: पिप्रीहि देवाम्̐ उशतो यविष्ठ इति स्विष्टकृतः पुरोनुवाक्या ये यजामहे \\ अग्निम्̐ स्विष्टकृतम् \ आयाड् अमुष्य \\ अयाड् अमुष्य \\ इति यथोक्तदेवता उपलक्ष्य \\ अग्ने यद् अद्य विशो अध्वरस्य होतर् इति यजति ॥
21.2.49.a.m: "Please the eager gods, O youngest one," is the introductory verse for the Sviṣṭakṛt; having named the deities as prescribed with: "We who sacrifice to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt...", "He has sacrificed to such-and-such...", "He has sacrificed to such-and-such...", he recites the offering verse: "O Agni, since today, the hotṛ of the clan of the sacrifice..."

21.2.50.a.s: gāyatryau vā saṃyājye brahmavarcasakāmasya kuryāt / triṣṭubhau vīryakāmasya / jagatyau paśukāmasyānuṣṭubhau pratiṣṭhākāmasya paṅktyau yajñakāmasya virājāv annakāmasyeti vijñāyate //
21.2.50.a.d: गायत्र्यौ वा संयाज्ये ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य कुर्यात् । त्रिष्टुभौ वीर्यकामस्य । जगत्यौ पशुकामस्यानुष्टुभौ प्रतिष्ठाकामस्य पङ्क्त्यौ यज्ञकामस्य विराजाव् अन्नकामस्येति विज्ञायते ॥
21.2.50.a.m: Or he should make the two saṃyājyā verses in the gāyatrī metre for one who desires spiritual lustre; in the triṣṭubh metre for one who desires vigor; in the jagatī metre for one who desires cattle; in the anuṣṭubh metre for one who desires firm standing; in the paṅkti metre for one who desires the sacrifice; in the virāj metre for one who desires food: thus it is known from the sacred texts.

21.2.51.a.m: Having sniffed the two joints of his fingers, he touches water.

21.2.52.a.s: athāsyādhvaryur antareṇāṅguṣṭhaprādeśanīṃ ca lepād upastṛṇāti svayam̐ hotā madhyato dvir ādatte 'dhvaryur vānyataral lepena cābhighārite vinigṛhṇāti cāṅgulibhiḥ //
21.2.52.a.d: अथास्याध्वर्युर् अन्तरेणाङ्गुष्ठप्रादेशनीं च लेपाद् उपस्तृणाति स्वयम्̐ होता मध्यतो द्विर् आदत्ते ऽध्वर्युर् वान्यतरल् लेपेन चाभिघारिते विनिगृह्णाति चाङ्गुलिभिः ॥
21.2.52.a.m: Then the adhvaryu spreads an under-layer [of clarified butter] between his thumb and forefinger from the residue. The hotṛ himself takes [the portion] twice from the middle, or the adhvaryu [takes it] on the other hand; and when it has been bastened with the residue, he holds it firmly with his fingers.

21.2.53.a.s: vijñāyate ca na prasṛtam̐ hastaṃ dhārayed yat prasṛtam̐ hastaṃ dhārayet prabhram̐śukā asmān paśavaḥ syuḥ //
21.2.53.a.d: विज्ञायते च न प्रसृतम्̐ हस्तं धारयेद् यत् प्रसृतम्̐ हस्तं धारयेत् प्रभ्रम्̐शुका अस्मान् पशवः स्युः ॥
21.2.53.a.m: And it is known from the sacred texts: 'He should not hold an outstretched hand; if he were to hold an outstretched hand, cattle would fall away from him.'

21.2.54.a.m: He should sit, as it were, gripping [it] tight; then he invokes the iḍā.

21.2.55.a.s: mukhena saṃmitā \\ upahūtam̐ rathaṃtaram ity upām̐śūktvā \\ upahūtām̐ ho ity ata uccair itarat //
21.2.55.a.d: मुखेन संमिता \\ उपहूतम्̐ रथंतरम् इत्य् उपाम्̐शूक्त्वा \\ उपहूताम्̐ हो इत्य् अत उच्चैर् इतरत् ॥
21.2.55.a.m: Holding [the portion] level with his mouth, having said inaudibly, 'Invoked is the rathaṃtara,' he utters the rest aloud from: 'Invoked, ho!'

21.2.56.a.s: yaṃ kāmayetāpaśuḥ syād iti parācīṃ tasyeḍām upahvayate / yaṃ kāmayeta paśumān syād iti pratīcīṃ tasyeḍām upahvayata / iḍopahūtā \\ upahūteḍā \\ iti tat pratīcyopahūyamānāyām //
21.2.56.a.d: यं कामयेतापशुः स्याद् इति पराचीं तस्येडाम् उपह्वयते । यं कामयेत पशुमान् स्याद् इति प्रतीचीं तस्येडाम् उपह्वयत । इडोपहूता \\ उपहूतेडा \\ इति तत् प्रतीच्योपहूयमानायाम् ॥
21.2.56.a.m: For one whom he desires to be without cattle, he invokes the iḍā turned away from him; for one whom he desires to possess cattle, he invokes the iḍā turned toward him. 'The iḍā is invoked; invoked is the iḍā'—that is when it is being invoked turned toward [him].

21.2.57.a.s: avāntareḍāṃ prāśnāti vācaspataye tvā hutaṃ prāśnāmi \ sadasaspataye tvā hutaṃ prāśnāmi \\ iti //
21.2.57.a.d: अवान्तरेडां प्राश्नाति वाचस्पतये त्वा हुतं प्राश्नामि \ सदसस्पतये त्वा हुतं प्राश्नामि \\ इति ॥
21.2.57.a.m: He consumes the intermediate iḍā with: 'To the lord of speech, thee offered, I consume; to the lord of the assembly, thee offered, I consume.'

21.2.58.a.s: caturdhā karṇikānāṃ hotṛbhāgaṃ prāśnāti pṛthivyai bhāgo 'si \\ iti //
21.2.58.a.d: चतुर्धा कर्णिकानां होतृभागं प्राश्नाति पृथिव्यै भागो ऽसि \\ इति ॥
21.2.58.a.m: Divided into four parts of the edge-pieces, he consumes the hotṛ's portion with: 'Thou art the portion for the earth.'

21.2.59.a.m: Having accepted the anvāhārya sacrificial gift and returned, he undertakes the after-offerings and subsequent rites.

21.2.60.a.m: At the after-offerings he does not make the 'ye yajāmahe' [recitation].

21.2.61.a.m: He begins [them] with the sacred utterances alone.

21.2.62.a.s: devān yaja \\ iti saṃpreṣite // devaṃ barhir vasuvane vasudheyasya vettu \\ iti yajati / devo narāśam̐so vasuvane vasudheyasya vettu iti dvitīyam / devo agniḥ sviṣṭakṛt \\ ity anavānam uttamam anūyājaṃ yajaty amatsate vā samata iti vijñāyate //
21.2.62.a.d: देवान् यज \\ इति संप्रेषिते ॥ देवं बर्हिर् वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेत्तु \\ इति यजति । देवो नराशम्̐सो वसुवने वसुधेयस्य वेत्तु इति द्वितीयम् । देवो अग्निः स्विष्टकृत् \\ इत्य् अनवानम् उत्तमम् अनूयाजं यजत्य् अमत्सते वा समत इति विज्ञायते ॥
21.2.62.a.m: When instructed with: 'Sacrifice to the gods,' he sacrifices with: 'May the divine sacred grass know of the gift of wealth in the winning of wealth.' The second with: 'May the divine Narāśaṃsa know of the gift of wealth in the winning of wealth.' With: 'May the divine Agni Sviṣṭakṛt...' he offers the last after-offering without taking breath, with 'they enjoyed' or 'they were delighted': so it is known from the sacred texts.

21.2.63.a.s: sūktā brūhi \\ iti saṃpreṣite \\ idaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī bhadram abhūt \\ iti sūktavākaṃ pratipadyate / sūktavāke yathoktadevatā upalakṣayati / upām̐śuyāje juṣatāvīvṛdhetākṛta \\ ity upāṃśūccair itarat //
21.2.63.a.d: सूक्ता ब्रूहि \\ इति संप्रेषिते \\ इदं द्यावापृथिवी भद्रम् अभूत् \\ इति सूक्तवाकं प्रतिपद्यते । सूक्तवाके यथोक्तदेवता उपलक्षयति । उपाम्̐शुयाजे जुषतावीवृधेताकृत \\ इत्य् उपांशूच्चैर् इतरत् ॥
21.2.63.a.m: When directed with: 'Recite the well-spoken words,' he undertakes the sūktavāka with: 'This has been auspicious, O Heaven and Earth.' In the sūktavāka he mentions the divinities as stated. With: 'In the inaudible offering may they take pleasure, may they thrive, they have done,' [he recites] inaudibly; the rest aloud.

21.2.64.a.s: āśāste 'yaṃ yajamāno 'sau \\ iti yajamānasya nāmanī gṛhṇāti / tṛtīyam̐ somayājinaḥ //
21.2.64.a.d: आशास्ते ऽयं यजमानो ऽसौ \\ इति यजमानस्य नामनी गृह्णाति । तृतीयम्̐ सोमयाजिनः ॥
21.2.64.a.m: With: 'This sacrificer N.N. hopes for...' he utters the two names of the sacrificer; a third name for a soma-sacrificer.

21.2.65.a.s: śaṃyor brūhi \\ iti saṃpreṣite tac chaṃ yor āvṛṇīmahe \\ iti śaṃyuvākaṃ pratipadyate //
21.2.65.a.d: शंयोर् ब्रूहि \\ इति संप्रेषिते तच् छं योर् आवृणीमहे \\ इति शंयुवाकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
21.2.65.a.m: When instructed with: 'Recite for bliss and peace,' he undertakes the śaṃyuvāka with: 'That bliss and peace we choose.'

21.2.66.a.m: Having spoken the śaṃyuvāka, he eats the remnants of the sacrificial oblation.

21.2.67.a.s: patnīsaṃyājeṣu vedam ādāya pratyaṅṅ etyāpareṇa gārhapatyam upaviśya patnīḥ saṃyājayati / upām̐śudhvānena vā \\ āpyāyasva \ saṃ te \\ iti somasya \\ iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam \\ tan nas turīpam iti tvaṣṭus \\ rākām aham \\ yās te rāke \\ iti rākāyāḥ sinīvāli yā supāṇir iti sinīvālyāḥ kuhūm aham \\ kuhūr devānām iti kuhvoḥ / devānāṃ patnīr uśatīr avantu nas \\ uta gnā viyantu devapatnīr iti devānāṃ patnīnām agnir hotā gṛhapatir \ vayam u tvā gṛhapate janānām ity agner gṛhapateḥ //
21.2.67.a.d: पत्नीसंयाजेषु वेदम् आदाय प्रत्यङ्ङ् एत्यापरेण गार्हपत्यम् उपविश्य पत्नीः संयाजयति । उपाम्̐शुध्वानेन वा \\ आप्यायस्व \ सं ते \\ इति सोमस्य \\ इह त्वष्टारम् अग्रियम् \\ तन् नस् तुरीपम् इति त्वष्टुस् \\ राकाम् अहम् \\ यास् ते राके \\ इति राकायाः सिनीवालि या सुपाणिर् इति सिनीवाल्याः कुहूम् अहम् \\ कुहूर् देवानाम् इति कुह्वोः । देवानां पत्नीर् उशतीर् अवन्तु नस् \\ उत ग्ना वियन्तु देवपत्नीर् इति देवानां पत्नीनाम् अग्निर् होता गृहपतिर् \ वयम् उ त्वा गृहपते जनानाम् इत्य् अग्नेर् गृहपतेः ॥
21.2.67.a.m: During the wife-offerings, taking the grass bunch and going west, having sat down behind the gārhapatya fire, he causes the wives [of the gods] to be offered sacrifice, or with an inaudible murmur: with 'Swell up,' 'May gather unto thee' for Soma; with 'Here Tvaṣṭṛ, the foremost,' 'Give us that virile fluid' for Tvaṣṭṛ; with 'Rākā I invoke,' 'Those thine, O Rākā' for Rākā; with 'Sinīvālī, who has fair hands' for Sinīvālī; with 'Kuhū I invoke,' 'Kuhū of the gods' for Kuhū; with 'May the willing wives of the gods protect us,' 'And may the women, the divine wives, depart' for the wives of the gods; with 'Agni the hotṛ, lord of the house,' 'And thee, O lord of the house of men, do we...' for Agni, lord of the house.

21.2.68.a.m: Having sniffed the two smeared finger-joints, he touches water.

21.2.69.a.m: He invokes the clarified-butter iḍā according to traditional text.

21.2.70.a.s: ūrdhvaṃ piṣṭalepaphalīkaraṇahomābhyām \\ vedo 'si \ vittir asi \\ iti vedaṃ patnyai prayacchati //
21.2.70.a.d: ऊर्ध्वं पिष्टलेपफलीकरणहोमाभ्याम् \\ वेदो ऽसि \ वित्तिर् असि \\ इति वेदं पत्न्यै प्रयच्छति ॥
21.2.70.a.m: After the oblations of the flour smearings and the chaff, he hands the grass bunch to the sacrificer's wife with: 'Thou art the veda; thou art attainment.'

21.2.71.a.s: vedo 'si \ vedase tvā \ vedo me vinda \\ iti vā //
21.2.71.a.d: वेदो ऽसि \ वेदसे त्वा \ वेदो मे विन्द \\ इति वा ॥
21.2.71.a.m: Or with: 'Thou art the veda; to the wise one thee; obtain for me knowledge.'

21.2.72.a.s: ghṛtavantaṃ kulāyinam iti vedam̐ hotā stṛṇann eti gārhapatyāt saṃtatam āhavanīyāt //
21.2.72.a.d: घृतवन्तं कुलायिनम् इति वेदम्̐ होता स्तृणन्न् एति गार्हपत्यात् संततम् आहवनीयात् ॥
21.2.72.a.m: With 'Full of ghee, having a nest...' the hotṛ walks while strewing the grass bunch continuously from the gārhapatya fire up to the āhavanīya fire.

21.2.73.a.m: He exits the way he came.

21.2.74.a.m: The hotṛ's duty in the New- and Full-Moon sacrifices is concluded.

21.3.1.a.m: We shall now explain the ancestral invocations.

21.3.2.a.s: ārṣeyaṃ vṛṇīte bandhor eva naity atho saṃtatyā iti vijñāyate //
21.3.2.a.d: आर्षेयं वृणीते बन्धोर् एव नैत्य् अथो संतत्या इति विज्ञायते ॥
21.3.2.a.m: 'He invokes the ancestral lineage of the ṛṣis: he does not depart from kinship, and also for continuity,' thus it is known from the sacred texts.

21.3.3.a.s: na devair manuṣyair ārṣeyaṃ vṛṇīta ṛṣibhir evārṣeyaṃ vṛṇīta iti vijñāyate //
21.3.3.a.d: न देवैर् मनुष्यैर् आर्षेयं वृणीत ऋषिभिर् एवार्षेयं वृणीत इति विज्ञायते ॥
21.3.3.a.m: 'He should not invoke the ancestral lineage by gods, nor by mortals; he should invoke the ancestral lineage by the ṛṣis alone,' thus it is known from the sacred texts.

21.3.4.a.s: ārṣeyam anvācaṣṭa ṛṣiṇā hi devāḥ puruṣam anubadhyanta iti vijñāyate //
21.3.4.a.d: आर्षेयम् अन्वाचष्ट ऋषिणा हि देवाः पुरुषम् अनुबध्यन्त इति विज्ञायते ॥
21.3.4.a.m: 'He recites the ancestral lineage, for through the ṛṣi the gods attach themselves to a man,' thus it is known from the sacred texts.

21.3.5.a.s: yo vā anyaḥ sann anyasyārṣeyaṃ vṛṇīte sa vā asya tad ṛṣir iṣṭaṃ vītaṃ vṛṅkta iti vijñāyate //
21.3.5.a.d: यो वा अन्यः सन्न् अन्यस्यार्षेयं वृणीते स वा अस्य तद् ऋषिर् इष्टं वीतं वृङ्क्त इति विज्ञायते ॥
21.3.5.a.m: 'Whoever, being one, invokes the ancestral lineage of another, his sacrifice and study that ṛṣi takes away,' thus it is known from the sacred texts.

21.3.6.a.s: ekaṃ vṛṇīte dvau vṛṇīte trīn vṛṇīte na caturo vṛṇīte na pañcātiprvṛṇīta iti vijñāyate //
21.3.6.a.d: एकं वृणीते द्वौ वृणीते त्रीन् वृणीते न चतुरो वृणीते न पञ्चातिप्र्वृणीत इति विज्ञायते ॥
21.3.6.a.m: 'He chooses one, he chooses two, he chooses three; he does not choose four, he does not choose more than five,' thus it is known from the sacred texts.

21.3.7.a.s: bhṛgūn evāgre vyākhyāsyāmaḥ // jāmadagnyā vatsās teṣāṃ pañcārṣeyo bhārgavacyāvanāpnavānaurvajāmadagnyeti jamadagnivad urvavad apnavānavac cyavanavad bhṛguvad iti tryārṣeyam u haike bhārgavaurvajāmadagnyeti jamadagnivad urvavad bhṛguvad ity eṣa evāvikṛto jāmālyaitiśāyanavirohitamāṇḍavyāvaṭamaṇḍubaidaretavāhaprācīnayogyānām athārṣṭiṣeṇānāṃ pañcārṣeyo bhārgavacyāvanāpnavānārṣṭiṣeṇānupety anūpavad ṛṣṭiṣeṇavad apnavānavac cyavanavad bhṛguvad iti / tryārṣeyam u haike bhārgavārṣṭiṣeṇānūpety anūpavad ṛṣṭiṣeṇavad bhṛguvad iti //
21.3.7.a.d: भृगून् एवाग्रे व्याख्यास्यामः ॥ जामदग्न्या वत्सास् तेषां पञ्चार्षेयो भार्गवच्यावनाप्नवानौर्वजामदग्न्येति जमदग्निवद् उर्ववद् अप्नवानवच् च्यवनवद् भृगुवद् इति त्र्यार्षेयम् उ हैके भार्गवौर्वजामदग्न्येति जमदग्निवद् उर्ववद् भृगुवद् इत्य् एष एवाविकृतो जामाल्यैतिशायनविरोहितमाण्डव्यावटमण्डुबैदरेतवाहप्राचीनयोग्यानाम् अथार्ष्टिषेणानां पञ्चार्षेयो भार्गवच्यावनाप्नवानार्ष्टिषेणानुपेत्य् अनूपवद् ऋष्टिषेणवद् अप्नवानवच् च्यवनवद् भृगुवद् इति । त्र्यार्षेयम् उ हैके भार्गवार्ष्टिषेणानूपेत्य् अनूपवद् ऋष्टिषेणवद् भृगुवद् इति ॥
21.3.7.a.m: First we shall explain the Bhṛgus: The Jāmadagnya Vatsas: their ancestral invocation has five ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Cyavana, of Apnavāna, of Ūrva, of Jamadagni!'—[and for the adhvaryu:] 'like Jamadagni, like Ūrva, like Apnavāna, like Cyavana, like Bhṛgu.' Some indeed say it has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Ūrva, of Jamadagni!'—'like Jamadagni, like Ūrva, like Bhṛgu.' This very same [formula] is unchanged for the Jāmālis, Aitiśāyanas, Virohitas, Māṇḍavyas, Āvaṭas, Maṇḍus, Baidas, Retavāhas, and Prācīnayogyas. Now for the Ārṣṭiṣeṇas, the ancestral invocation has five ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Cyavana, of Apnavāna, of Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, of Anūpa!'—'like Anūpa, like Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, like Apnavāna, like Cyavana, like Bhṛgu.' And some say it has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, of Anūpa!'—'like Anūpa, like Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, like Bhṛgu.'

21.3.7.b.s: atha vītahavyā yāskavādhūlamaunamaukarajātavāhās teṣāṃ tryārṣeyo bhārgavavaitahavyasāvedaseti savedovad vītahavyavad bhṛguvad iti //
21.3.7.b.d: अथ वीतहव्या यास्कवाधूलमौनमौकरजातवाहास् तेषां त्र्यार्षेयो भार्गववैतहव्यसावेदसेति सवेदोवद् वीतहव्यवद् भृगुवद् इति ॥
21.3.7.b.m: Now the Vītahavyas, Yāskas, Vādhūlas, Maunas, Maukaras, and Jātavāhas: their ancestral invocation has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Vītahavya, of Savedas!'—'like Savedas, like Vītahavya, like Bhṛgu.'

21.3.7.c.s: atha vainyāḥ pārthās teṣāṃ tryārṣeyo bhārgavavainyapārtheti pṛthuvad venavad bhṛguvad iti //
21.3.7.c.d: अथ वैन्याः पार्थास् तेषां त्र्यार्षेयो भार्गववैन्यपार्थेति पृथुवद् वेनवद् भृगुवद् इति ॥
21.3.7.c.m: Now the Vainyas and Pārthas: their ancestral invocation has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Vena, of Pṛthu!'—'like Pṛthu, like Vena, like Bhṛgu.'

21.3.7.d.s: atha gārtsamadāḥ śunakās teṣām ekārṣeyo gārtsamadeti hotā gṛtsamadavad ity adhvaryuḥ / atha vāghryaśvā mitrayuvas teṣām ekārṣeyo vāghryaśveti hotā vaghryaśvavad ity adhvaryuḥ //
21.3.7.d.d: अथ गार्त्समदाः शुनकास् तेषाम् एकार्षेयो गार्त्समदेति होता गृत्समदवद् इत्य् अध्वर्युः । अथ वाघ्र्यश्वा मित्रयुवस् तेषाम् एकार्षेयो वाघ्र्यश्वेति होता वघ्र्यश्ववद् इत्य् अध्वर्युः ॥
21.3.7.d.m: Now the Gārtsamadas and Śunakas: their ancestral invocation has one ṛṣi: 'O descendant of Gṛtsamada!'—the hotṛ [says; and] 'like Gṛtsamada'—the adhvaryu [says]. Now the Vāghryaśvas and Mitrayus: their ancestral invocation has one ṛṣi: 'O descendant of Vadhryaśva!'—the hotṛ [says; and] 'like Vadhryaśva'—the adhvaryu [says].

21.3.8.a.m: Thus the Bhṛgus have been explained.

21.3.9.a.s: athāto 'ṅgirasām ayāsyā gautamās teṣāṃ tryārṣeya āṅgirasāyāsyagautameti gotamavad ayāsyavad aṅgirovad iti / athaitathyā gautamās teṣāṃ tryārṣeya āṅgirasautathyagautameti gotamavad utathyavad aṅgirovad iti / athauśijā gautamās teṣāṃ tryārṣeya āṅgirasauśijakākṣīvateti kakṣīvad vaduśijavad aṅgirovad iti / atha vāmadevā gautamās teṣāṃ tryarṣeya āṅgirasavāmadevabārhadutkheti bṛhadukthavad vāmadevavad aṅgirovad iti //
21.3.9.a.d: अथातो ऽङ्गिरसाम् अयास्या गौतमास् तेषां त्र्यार्षेय आङ्गिरसायास्यगौतमेति गोतमवद् अयास्यवद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति । अथैतथ्या गौतमास् तेषां त्र्यार्षेय आङ्गिरसौतथ्यगौतमेति गोतमवद् उतथ्यवद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति । अथौशिजा गौतमास् तेषां त्र्यार्षेय आङ्गिरसौशिजकाक्षीवतेति कक्षीवद् वदुशिजवद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति । अथ वामदेवा गौतमास् तेषां त्र्यर्षेय आङ्गिरसवामदेवबार्हदुत्खेति बृहदुक्थवद् वामदेववद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति ॥
21.3.9.a.m: Now next of the Aṅgirases: the Ayāsya Gautamas: their ancestral invocation has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Ayāsya, of Gotama!'—'like Gotama, like Ayāsya, like Aṅgiras.' Now the Autathya Gautamas: their ancestral invocation has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Utathya, of Gotama!'—'like Gotama, like Utathya, like Aṅgiras.' Now the Auśija Gautamas: their ancestral invocation has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Uśij, of Kakṣīvat!'—'like Kakṣīvat, like Uśij, like Aṅgiras.' Now the Vāmadeva Gautamas: their ancestral invocation has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Vāmadeva, of Bṛhaduktha!'—'like Bṛhaduktha, like Vāmadeva, like Aṅgiras.'

21.3.10.a.s: atha bharadvājānāṃ tryārṣeya āṅgirasabārhaspatyabhāradvājeti bharadvājavad bṛhaspativad aṅgirovad iti / eṣa evāvikṛtastuthyāgniveśyaurjayānānāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca stambhastambaśabdānām / atharkṣāṇāṃ pañcārṣeya āṅgirasabārhaspatyabhāradvājavāndanamātavacaseti matavacovad vandanavad bharadvājavad bṛhaspativad aṅgirovad iti / tryārṣeyam u haika āṅgirasavāndanamātavacaseti / matavacovad vandanavad aṅgirovad iti / atha dvyāmuṣyāyaṇānāṃ kulānāṃ yathā śauṅgaśaiśirayo bharadvājāḥ śuṅgāḥ katāḥ śaiśirayas teṣāṃ pañcārṣeya āṅgirasabārhaspatyadbharadvājakātyākṣilety akṣilavat katavad bharadvājavad bṛhaspativad aṅgirovad iti tryārṣeyam u haika āṅgirasakātyākṣilety akṣilavat katavad aṅgirovad iti //
21.3.10.a.d: अथ भरद्वाजानां त्र्यार्षेय आङ्गिरसबार्हस्पत्यभारद्वाजेति भरद्वाजवद् बृहस्पतिवद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति । एष एवाविकृतस्तुथ्याग्निवेश्यौर्जयानानां सर्वेषां च स्तम्भस्तम्बशब्दानाम् । अथर्क्षाणां पञ्चार्षेय आङ्गिरसबार्हस्पत्यभारद्वाजवान्दनमातवचसेति मतवचोवद् वन्दनवद् भरद्वाजवद् बृहस्पतिवद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति । त्र्यार्षेयम् उ हैक आङ्गिरसवान्दनमातवचसेति । मतवचोवद् वन्दनवद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति । अथ द्व्यामुष्यायणानां कुलानां यथा शौङ्गशैशिरयो भरद्वाजाः शुङ्गाः कताः शैशिरयस् तेषां पञ्चार्षेय आङ्गिरसबार्हस्पत्यद्भरद्वाजकात्याक्षिलेत्य् अक्षिलवत् कतवद् भरद्वाजवद् बृहस्पतिवद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति त्र्यार्षेयम् उ हैक आङ्गिरसकात्याक्षिलेत्य् अक्षिलवत् कतवद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति ॥
21.3.10.a.m: Now, for the Bharadvājas, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Bṛhaspati, Bharadvāja!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Bharadvāja, like Bṛhaspati, like Aṅgiras' [by the adhvaryu]. This very [formula] is unchanged for the Tuthiyas, the Āgniveśyas, the Aurjayānas, and all those whose names end in -stamba or -stambha. Now, for the Ṛkṣas, there is an ancestral invocation of five ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Bṛhaspati, descendant of Bharadvāja, descendant of Vandana, descendant of Mātavacas!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Mātavacas, like Vandana, like Bharadvāja, like Bṛhaspati, like Aṅgiras' [by the adhvaryu]. Some indeed say it has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Vandana, descendant of Mātavacas!' [and] 'Like Mātavacas, like Vandana, like Aṅgiras.' Now, for the lineages of double descent, such as the Śauṅga-Śaiśirayas—the Bharadvājas being Śuṅgas, and the Katas being Śaiśirayas—theirs has an ancestral invocation of five ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Bṛhaspati, descendant of Bharadvāja, descendant of Kata, descendant of Akṣila!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Akṣila, like Kata, like Bharadvāja, like Bṛhaspati, like Aṅgiras' [by the adhvaryu]. Some indeed say it has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Kata, descendant of Akṣila!' [and] 'Like Akṣila, like Kata, like Aṅgiras.'

21.3.10.b.s: atha gargāṇāṃ tryārṣeya āṅgirasagārgyaśainyeti śinivad gargavad aṅgirovad iti / bhāradvājam u haike 'ṅgirasaḥ sthāne bhāradvājagārgyaśainyeti śinivad gargavad bharadvājavad iti / atha kapīnāṃ tryārṣeya āṅgirasamāhayyavaurukṣayyety urukṣayyavan mahayyuvad aṅgirovad iti tarasvām̐s tilo viduḥ śāluḥ patañjalir bhūyasīr dadvakīr jalandūḥ / kaper aṣṭavidhāḥ prajāḥ //
21.3.10.b.d: अथ गर्गाणां त्र्यार्षेय आङ्गिरसगार्ग्यशैन्येति शिनिवद् गर्गवद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति । भारद्वाजम् उ हैके ऽङ्गिरसः स्थाने भारद्वाजगार्ग्यशैन्येति शिनिवद् गर्गवद् भरद्वाजवद् इति । अथ कपीनां त्र्यार्षेय आङ्गिरसमाहय्यवौरुक्षय्येत्य् उरुक्षय्यवन् महय्युवद् अङ्गिरोवद् इति तरस्वाम्̐स् तिलो विदुः शालुः पतञ्जलिर् भूयसीर् दद्वकीर् जलन्दूः । कपेर् अष्टविधाः प्रजाः ॥
21.3.10.b.m: Now, for the Gargas, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Garga, descendant of Śini!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Śini, like Garga, like Aṅgiras' [by the adhvaryu]. Some indeed say 'descendant of Bharadvāja' in place of 'descendant of Aṅgiras': 'O descendant of Bharadvāja, descendant of Garga, descendant of Śini!' [and] 'Like Śini, like Garga, like Bharadvāja.' Now, for the Kapis, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Mahayyu, descendant of Urukṣaya!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Urukṣaya, like Mahayyu, like Aṅgiras' [by the adhvaryu]. Tarasvin, Tila, Vidu, Śālu, Patañjali, Bhūyasī, Dadvakī, Jalandu—[these are] the eightfold progenies of Kapi.

21.3.11.a.s: athātrīṇāṃ tryārṣeya ātreyārcanānasaśyāvāśveti śvāvāśvavad arcanānasavad atrivad iti / atha gaviṣṭhirāṇāṃ tryārṣeya ātreyārcanānasagāviṣṭhireti gaviṣṭhiravad arcanānasavad atrivad iti / eṣa evāvikṛto vāmarathyasumaṅgalabījavāpānām //
21.3.11.a.d: अथात्रीणां त्र्यार्षेय आत्रेयार्चनानसश्यावाश्वेति श्वावाश्ववद् अर्चनानसवद् अत्रिवद् इति । अथ गविष्ठिराणां त्र्यार्षेय आत्रेयार्चनानसगाविष्ठिरेति गविष्ठिरवद् अर्चनानसवद् अत्रिवद् इति । एष एवाविकृतो वामरथ्यसुमङ्गलबीजवापानाम् ॥
21.3.11.a.m: Now, for the Atris, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Atri, descendant of Arcanānas, descendant of Śyāvāśva!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Śyāvāśva, like Arcanānas, like Atri' [by the adhvaryu]. Now, for the Gaviṣṭhiras, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Atri, descendant of Arcanānas, descendant of Gaviṣṭhira!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Gaviṣṭhira, like Arcanānas, like Atri' [by the adhvaryu]. This very [formula] is unchanged for the Vāmarathyas, Sumaṅgalas, and Bījavāpas.

21.3.12.a.s: atha viśvāmitrāṇāṃ devarātāścikitakālabavamanutantubabhruyajñavalkaulontyermaribṛhadagnisāṃśityavārakitārakāyaṇaśālāvatās teṣāṃ tryārṣeyo vaiśvāmitradaivarātaudaleti udalavad devarātavad viśvāmitravad iti /
21.3.12.a.d: अथ विश्वामित्राणां देवराताश्चिकितकालबवमनुतन्तुबभ्रुयज्ञवल्कौलोन्त्येर्मरिबृहदग्निसांशित्यवारकितारकायणशालावतास् तेषां त्र्यार्षेयो वैश्वामित्रदैवरातौदलेति उदलवद् देवरातवद् विश्वामित्रवद् इति ।
21.3.12.a.m: Now, for the Viśvāmitras: the Devarātas, Cikitas, Kālabavas, Manutantus, Babhrus, Yajñavalkas, Ulontis, Irmaris, Bṛhadagnis, Sāṃśityas, Vārakis, Tārakayāṇas, and Śālāvats. For them, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, descendant of Devarāta, descendant of Udala!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Udala, like Devarāta, like Viśvāmitra' [by the adhvaryu].

21.3.12.b.s: atha śraumatakāmakāyanās teṣāṃ tryārṣeyo vaiśvāmitramādhucchandasadhānaṃjayyeti dhanaṃjayavan madhucchandovad viśvāmitravad iti / athāṣṭakā lohitās teṣāṃ dvyārṣeyo vaiśvāmitrāṣṭaketi / aṣṭakavad viśvāmitravad iti / atha pūraṇāḥ pāridhāpayantyas teṣāṃ dvyārṣeyo vaiśvāmitrapauraṇeti / pūraṇavad viśvāmitravad iti / atha katās teṣāṃ tryārṣeyo vaiśvāmitrakātyākṣileti / akṣilavat katavad viśvāmitravad iti / athāghamarṣaṇāḥ kuśikās teṣāṃ tryārṣeyo vaiśvāmitrāghamarṣaṇakauśiketi / kuśikavad aghamarṣaṇavad viśvāmitravad iti //
21.3.12.b.d: अथ श्रौमतकामकायनास् तेषां त्र्यार्षेयो वैश्वामित्रमाधुच्छन्दसधानंजय्येति धनंजयवन् मधुच्छन्दोवद् विश्वामित्रवद् इति । अथाष्टका लोहितास् तेषां द्व्यार्षेयो वैश्वामित्राष्टकेति । अष्टकवद् विश्वामित्रवद् इति । अथ पूरणाः पारिधापयन्त्यस् तेषां द्व्यार्षेयो वैश्वामित्रपौरणेति । पूरणवद् विश्वामित्रवद् इति । अथ कतास् तेषां त्र्यार्षेयो वैश्वामित्रकात्याक्षिलेति । अक्षिलवत् कतवद् विश्वामित्रवद् इति । अथाघमर्षणाः कुशिकास् तेषां त्र्यार्षेयो वैश्वामित्राघमर्षणकौशिकेति । कुशिकवद् अघमर्षणवद् विश्वामित्रवद् इति ॥
21.3.12.b.m: Now, for the Śraumata-Kāmakāyanas, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, descendant of Madhucchandas, descendant of Dhanañjaya!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Dhanañjaya, like Madhucchandas, like Viśvāmitra' [by the adhvaryu]. Now, for the Aṣṭaka-Lohitas, there is an ancestral invocation of two ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, descendant of Aṣṭaka!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Aṣṭaka, like Viśvāmitra' [by the adhvaryu]. Now, for the Pūraṇas and Pāridhāpayantis, there is an ancestral invocation of two ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, descendant of Pūraṇa!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Pūraṇa, like Viśvāmitra' [by the adhvaryu]. Now, for the Katas, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, descendant of Kata, descendant of Akṣila!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Akṣila, like Kata, like Viśvāmitra' [by the adhvaryu]. Now, for the Aghamarṣaṇas and Kuśikas, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, descendant of Aghamarṣaṇa, descendant of Kuśika!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Kuśika, like Aghamarṣaṇa, like Viśvāmitra' [by the adhvaryu].

21.3.13.a.s: atha kaśyapānāṃ tryārṣeyaḥ kāśyapāvatsāranaidhruveti nidhrubavad avatsāravat kaśyapavad ity eṣa evāvikṛto dhaumyābhiṣeṇyamāṭharāṇām / atha rebhāṇāṃ tryārṣeyaḥ kāśyapāvatsāraraibhyeti / rebhavad avatsāravat kaśyapavad iti // atha śaṇḍilānāṃ dvyārṣeyo daivalāsiteti / asitavad devalavad iti / tryārṣeyam u haike kāśyapadaivalāsiteti / asitavad devalavat kaśyapavad iti / dvyārṣeyās tv evaṃ nyāyena //
21.3.13.a.d: अथ कश्यपानां त्र्यार्षेयः काश्यपावत्सारनैध्रुवेति निध्रुबवद् अवत्सारवत् कश्यपवद् इत्य् एष एवाविकृतो धौम्याभिषेण्यमाठराणाम् । अथ रेभाणां त्र्यार्षेयः काश्यपावत्साररैभ्येति । रेभवद् अवत्सारवत् कश्यपवद् इति ॥ अथ शण्डिलानां द्व्यार्षेयो दैवलासितेति । असितवद् देवलवद् इति । त्र्यार्षेयम् उ हैके काश्यपदैवलासितेति । असितवद् देवलवत् कश्यपवद् इति । द्व्यार्षेयास् त्व् एवं न्यायेन ॥
21.3.13.a.m: Now, for the Kaśyapas, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Kaśyapa, descendant of Avatsāra, descendant of Nidhruva!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Nidhruva, like Avatsāra, like Kaśyapa' [by the adhvaryu]. This very [formula] is unchanged for the Dhaumyas, Abhiṣeṇyas, and Māṭharas. Now, for the Rebhas, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Kaśyapa, descendant of Avatsāra, descendant of Rebha!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Rebha, like Avatsāra, like Kaśyapa' [by the adhvaryu]. Now, for the Śaṇḍilas, there is an ancestral invocation of two ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Devala, descendant of Asita!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Asita, like Devala' [by the adhvaryu]. Some indeed say it has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Kaśyapa, descendant of Devala, descendant of Asita!' [and] 'Like Asita, like Devala, like Kaśyapa.' But by rule they have an ancestral invocation of two ṛṣis.

21.3.14.a.s: ekārṣeyā vāsiṣṭhā anyatropamanyuparāśarakuṇḍinebhyo vāsiṣṭheti hotā vasiṣṭhavad ity adhvaryuḥ / athopamanyūnāṃ tryārṣeyo vāsiṣṭhaindrapramadābharadvaso iti / ābharadvasuvad indrapramadavad vasiṣṭhavad iti / atha parāśarāṇāṃ tryārṣeyo vāsiṣṭhaśāktyaparārāśaryeti / parāśaravac chaktivad vasiṣṭhavad iti / atha kuṇḍinānāṃ tryārṣeyo vāsiṣṭhamaitrāvaruṇakauṇḍinyeti / kuṇḍinavan mitrāvaruṇavad vasiṣṭhavad iti / atha saṃkṛtipūtimāṣataṇḍināṃ tryārṣeyaḥ śāktyasāṃkṛtyagaurivīteti / gurivītavat saṃkṛtivac chaktivad iti //
21.3.14.a.d: एकार्षेया वासिष्ठा अन्यत्रोपमन्युपराशरकुण्डिनेभ्यो वासिष्ठेति होता वसिष्ठवद् इत्य् अध्वर्युः । अथोपमन्यूनां त्र्यार्षेयो वासिष्ठैन्द्रप्रमदाभरद्वसो इति । आभरद्वसुवद् इन्द्रप्रमदवद् वसिष्ठवद् इति । अथ पराशराणां त्र्यार्षेयो वासिष्ठशाक्त्यपराराशर्येति । पराशरवच् छक्तिवद् वसिष्ठवद् इति । अथ कुण्डिनानां त्र्यार्षेयो वासिष्ठमैत्रावरुणकौण्डिन्येति । कुण्डिनवन् मित्रावरुणवद् वसिष्ठवद् इति । अथ संकृतिपूतिमाषतण्डिनां त्र्यार्षेयः शाक्त्यसांकृत्यगौरिवीतेति । गुरिवीतवत् संकृतिवच् छक्तिवद् इति ॥
21.3.14.a.m: The Vāsiṣṭhas have an ancestral invocation of one ṛṣi, except for the Upamanyus, the Parāśaras, and the Kuṇḍinas: 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha!' says the hotṛ; 'Like Vasiṣṭha' says the adhvaryu. Now, for the Upamanyus, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha, descendant of Indrapramada, descendant of Ābharadvasu!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Ābharadvasu, like Indrapramada, like Vasiṣṭha' [by the adhvaryu]. Now, for the Parāśaras, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha, descendant of Śakti, descendant of Parāśara!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Parāśara, like Śakti, like Vasiṣṭha' [by the adhvaryu]. Now, for the Kuṇḍinas, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha, descendant of Mitrāvaruṇa, descendant of Kuṇḍina!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Kuṇḍin, like Mitrāvaruṇa, like Vasiṣṭha' [by the adhvaryu]. Now, for the Saṅkṛtis, Pūtimāṣas, and Taṇḍins, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Śakti, descendant of Saṅkṛti, descendant of Gaurivīti!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Gaurivīti, like Saṅkṛti, like Śakti' [by the adhvaryu].

21.3.15.a.s: athāgastīnām ekārṣeya āgastyeti hotāgastivad ity adhvaryuḥ / tryārṣeyam u haike āgastyadārḍhyacyutaidhmavāheti / idhmavāhavad dṛḍhacyutavad agastivad iti //
21.3.15.a.d: अथागस्तीनाम् एकार्षेय आगस्त्येति होतागस्तिवद् इत्य् अध्वर्युः । त्र्यार्षेयम् उ हैके आगस्त्यदार्ढ्यच्युतैध्मवाहेति । इध्मवाहवद् दृढच्युतवद् अगस्तिवद् इति ॥
21.3.15.a.m: Now, for the Agastis, there is an ancestral invocation of one ṛṣi: 'O descendant of Agasti!' says the hotṛ; 'Like Agasti' says the adhvaryu. Some indeed say it has three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Agasti, descendant of Dṛḍhacyuta, descendant of Idhmavāha!' [and] 'Like Idhmavāha, like Dṛḍhacyuta, like Agasti.'

21.3.16.a.s: atha kṣatriyāṇāṃ tryārṣeyo mānavaiḍapaurūravaseti / purūravovad iḍavad manuvad iti / atha yadi ha sārṣāḥ pravṛṇīrann eka evaiṣāṃ pravaro yady u vai pṛthak pravṛṇīran yeṣām u ha mantrakṛto na syuḥ sapurohitapravarās te / atha yeṣāṃ syur apurohitapravarās te sapurohitapravarās tv evaṃ nyāyenaikārṣeyā viśo vātsapreti hotā vatsapravad ity adhvaryuḥ //
21.3.16.a.d: अथ क्षत्रियाणां त्र्यार्षेयो मानवैडपौरूरवसेति । पुरूरवोवद् इडवद् मनुवद् इति । अथ यदि ह सार्षाः प्रवृणीरन्न् एक एवैषां प्रवरो यद्य् उ वै पृथक् प्रवृणीरन् येषाम् उ ह मन्त्रकृतो न स्युः सपुरोहितप्रवरास् ते । अथ येषां स्युर् अपुरोहितप्रवरास् ते सपुरोहितप्रवरास् त्व् एवं न्यायेनैकार्षेया विशो वात्सप्रेति होता वत्सप्रवद् इत्य् अध्वर्युः ॥
21.3.16.a.m: Now, for the kṣatriyas, there is an ancestral invocation of three ṛṣis: 'O descendant of Manu, descendant of Iḍā, descendant of Purūravas!' [by the hotṛ], and 'Like Purūravas, like Iḍā, like Manu' [by the adhvaryu]. Now, if they choose together, their ancestral invocation is one only; but if they choose separately, those among them who have no mantra-composers [among their ancestors] use the ancestral invocation of their purohita. Now, those who have them do not use the ancestral invocation of their purohita; but by rule, they use the ancestral invocation of their purohita. The vaiśyas have an ancestral invocation of one ṛṣi: 'O descendant of Vatsaprī!' says the hotṛ; 'Like Vatsaprī' says the adhvaryu.

21.3.17.a.m: Now, for one whose family is unknown, [the sacrifice is performed] with the ancestral invocation of his purohita, or with the ancestral invocation of his teacher.

21.3.18.a.s: atha ha tāṇḍina ekārṣeyam̐ sārvavarṇikam̐ samāmananti mānaveti hotā manuvad ity adhvaryuḥ / mānavyo hi prajās \\ iti hi brāhmaṇam iti hi brāhmaṇam //
21.3.18.a.d: अथ ह ताण्डिन एकार्षेयम्̐ सार्ववर्णिकम्̐ समामनन्ति मानवेति होता मनुवद् इत्य् अध्वर्युः । मानव्यो हि प्रजास् \\ इति हि ब्राह्मणम् इति हि ब्राह्मणम् ॥
21.3.18.a.m: Now, the Tāṇḍins prescribe an ancestral invocation of one ṛṣi common to all varṇas: 'O descendant of Manu!' says the hotṛ; 'Like Manu' says the adhvaryu. 'For creatures are descended from Manu,' says the Brāhmaṇa; 'thus says the Brāhmaṇa.'

22.1.1.a.s: kāmyaiḥ paśubhir amāvāsyāṃ paurṇamāsīṃ vā sam̐sthāpya yajeta / te brāhmaṇavyākhyātāḥ //
22.1.1.a.d: काम्यैः पशुभिर् अमावास्यां पौर्णमासीं वा सम्̐स्थाप्य यजेत । ते ब्राह्मणव्याख्याताः ॥
22.1.1.a.m: Having concluded the New Moon or Full Moon sacrifice, one should sacrifice with the optional animal sacrifices. They are explained in the Brāhmaṇa.

22.1.1.b.m: Their ritual procedure is explained by the independent animal sacrifice.

22.1.3.a.s: sarveṣv ābhicārikeṣu śaramayaṃ barhir vaibhītaka idhmo lohitoṣṇīṣā lohitavasanā nivītā ṛtvijaḥ pracaranti //
22.1.3.a.d: सर्वेष्व् आभिचारिकेषु शरमयं बर्हिर् वैभीतक इध्मो लोहितोष्णीषा लोहितवसना निवीता ऋत्विजः प्रचरन्ति ॥
22.1.3.a.m: In all sorcery rites, the sacred grass consists of reed grass, the firewood is made of vibhītaka wood, and the priests perform the rites wearing red turbans, red garments, and the cord suspended round the neck.

22.1.4.a.s: vāyavyam̐ śvetam ālabheta bhūtikāma iti yathāsamāmnātam //
22.1.4.a.d: वायव्यम्̐ श्वेतम् आलभेत भूतिकाम इति यथासमाम्नातम् ॥
22.1.4.a.m: 'One desiring prosperity should seize a white [victim] dedicated to Vāyu,' as it is handed down by tradition.

22.1.5.a.s: teṣām āvāpikeṣu sthāneṣu yathādevatam̐ ṣaḍ ṛco nidadhāti pīvo'nnām̐ rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhās \\ iti / etāni yathārūpaṃ yathādevatam āmnātāni bhavanti //
22.1.5.a.d: तेषाम् आवापिकेषु स्थानेषु यथादेवतम्̐ षड् ऋचो निदधाति पीवोऽन्नाम्̐ रयिवृधः सुमेधास् \\ इति । एतानि यथारूपं यथादेवतम् आम्नातानि भवन्ति ॥
22.1.5.a.m: In their variable places, he inserts six verses according to the deity: 'Fat with food, increasers of wealth, the wise...'; these are handed down according to form and deity.

22.1.6.a.m: [The word] 'malhāḥ' means having fleshy wattles under the neck.

22.1.7.a.s: viṣama ālabheteti viṣamaṃ devayajanam adhyavasyati paśuṃ vā viṣama ālabheta //
22.1.7.a.d: विषम आलभेतेति विषमं देवयजनम् अध्यवस्यति पशुं वा विषम आलभेत ॥
22.1.7.a.m: 'He should seize [the victim] on an uneven [ground]' means that he selects an uneven sacrificial site, or he should seize the animal on uneven [ground].

22.1.8.a.m: 'Paryāriṇī' means one that has repeatedly miscarried.

22.1.9.a.s: sphyo yūpa iti sphyākṛtiyūpa āgnyāgāriko vā //
22.1.9.a.d: स्फ्यो यूप इति स्फ्याकृतियूप आग्न्यागारिको वा ॥
22.1.9.a.m: 'The wooden sword is the sacrificial post' means a sacrificial post shaped like a wooden sword, or one that belongs to the fire-sanctuary.

22.1.10.a.s: tvāṣṭraṃ vaḍavam iti yaṃ pumām̐sam̐ santam ārohanti //
22.1.10.a.d: त्वाष्ट्रं वडवम् इति यं पुमाम्̐सम्̐ सन्तम् आरोहन्ति ॥
22.1.10.a.m: 'A stallion dedicated to Tvaṣṭṛ' means a male that mounts [the mares].

22.1.11.a.s: apāṃ cauṣadhīnāṃ ca saṃdhau \\ iti prāvṛṣi śaratpratipattau vā / api vāpāṃ cauṣadhīnāṃ ca saṃdhau //
22.1.11.a.d: अपां चौषधीनां च संधौ \\ इति प्रावृषि शरत्प्रतिपत्तौ वा । अपि वापां चौषधीनां च संधौ ॥
22.1.11.a.m: 'At the junction of the waters and the plants' means in the rainy season or at the onset of autumn; or rather, at the actual confluence of the waters and the plants.

22.1.12.a.s: viśākho yūpa iti yad ūrdhvaṃ raśanāyās tad viśākhaṃ yad vopary ubhe śākhe aṣṭāśrī sacasāle syātām //
22.1.12.a.d: विशाखो यूप इति यद् ऊर्ध्वं रशनायास् तद् विशाखं यद् वोपर्य् उभे शाखे अष्टाश्री सचसाले स्याताम् ॥
22.1.12.a.m: With the words, 'The sacrificial post has two branches,' [it means that] whatever is above the rope is two-branched, or above both branches should have eight corners and have top-rings.

22.1.13.a.s: ṛṣabhe goṣu jīrṇe yūnaḥ karṇam ājapet piśaṅgarūpas tan nas turīpam iti //
22.1.13.a.d: ऋषभे गोषु जीर्णे यूनः कर्णम् आजपेत् पिशङ्गरूपस् तन् नस् तुरीपम् इति ॥
22.1.13.a.m: When the bull among the cows is old, he should whisper into the ear of a young [bull]: 'Having a tawny form, that offspring of ours...'

22.1.14.a.s: athainaṃ goṣv apisṛjati \\ etaṃ yuvānam iti //
22.1.14.a.d: अथैनं गोष्व् अपिसृजति \\ एतं युवानम् इति ॥
22.1.14.a.m: Then he releases him among the cows with: 'This young [bull]...'

22.1.15.a.s: jīrṇam ālabhate // prājāpatyam aindraṃ tvāṣṭraṃ vā namo mahimne \\ ity upākaraṇe 'nuvartayate //
22.1.15.a.d: जीर्णम् आलभते ॥ प्राजापत्यम् ऐन्द्रं त्वाष्ट्रं वा नमो महिम्ने \\ इत्य् उपाकरणे ऽनुवर्तयते ॥
22.1.15.a.m: He immolates the old one. Dedicated to Prajāpati, Indra, or Tvaṣṭṛ, he adds at the dedication: 'Homage to greatness!'

22.1.16.a.s: tṛtīyayā vapāṃ juhoti / caturthyā haviḥ / pañcamyā sauviṣṭakṛtam //
22.1.16.a.d: तृतीयया वपां जुहोति । चतुर्थ्या हविः । पञ्चम्या सौविष्टकृतम् ॥
22.1.16.a.m: With the third [verse] he offers the omentum; with the fourth, the sacrificial oblation; with the fifth, the Sviṣṭakṛt offering.

22.1.17.a.m: Having assigned an eight-pot-sherd [sacrificial cake] for Agni, he immolates a barren she-goat.

22.1.18.a.s: vāyavyam ālabheta bhūtikāma ity uktāni daivatāni //
22.1.18.a.d: वायव्यम् आलभेत भूतिकाम इत्य् उक्तानि दैवतानि ॥
22.1.18.a.m: 'One desiring prosperity should immolate an animal for Vāyu'—thus the deities are declared.

22.1.19.a.s: ajāṃ vaśām ālabhamāne \\ ā vāyo bhūṣa \\ iti vāyavyā yopākaroti //
22.1.19.a.d: अजां वशाम् आलभमाने \\ आ वायो भूष \\ इति वायव्या योपाकरोति ॥
22.1.19.a.m: When immolating the barren she-goat, he dedicates it with the verse addressed to Vāyu: 'O Vāyu, come adorn...'

22.1.20.a.s: ākūtyai tvā kāmāya tvā \\ iti paryagnau kriyāmāṇe 'pāvyāni juhoti //
22.1.20.a.d: आकूत्यै त्वा कामाय त्वा \\ इति पर्यग्नौ क्रियामाणे ऽपाव्यानि जुहोति ॥
22.1.20.a.m: While the carrying of fire around [the victim] is being performed, he offers the Apāvya libations with: 'To intention, to you; to desire, to you...'

22.1.21.a.s: tvaṃ turīyā vaśinī vaśāsi \\ ity udīcīṃ nīyamānām anumantrayate //
22.1.21.a.d: त्वं तुरीया वशिनी वशासि \\ इत्य् उदीचीं नीयमानाम् अनुमन्त्रयते ॥
22.1.21.a.m: As she is being led toward the north, he follows her with the mantra: 'You are the fourth commanding barren cow...'

22.1.22.a.m: As she is being struck down, [he recites]: 'You are a she-goat abiding in wealth.'

22.1.23.a.m: With: 'Stretching the thread...' he offers the omentum.

22.1.24.a.m: With: 'Weave without fault...' [he offers] the sacrificial oblation.

22.1.25.a.s: manaso havir asi \\ iti haviḥśeṣān prāśnanti //
22.1.25.a.d: मनसो हविर् असि \\ इति हविःशेषान् प्राश्नन्ति ॥
22.1.25.a.m: They consume the remnants of the sacrificial oblation with: 'You are the oblation of the mind...'

22.1.26.a.s: sā vā eṣā trayāṇām evāvaruddhā \\ iti vijñāyate //
22.1.26.a.d: सा वा एषा त्रयाणाम् एवावरुद्धा \\ इति विज्ञायते ॥
22.1.26.a.m: 'That [cow/she-goat] indeed is obtained only for three,' thus it is known from sacred tradition.

22.1.27.a.s: tasyai vā etasyā ekam evādevayajanaṃ yad ālabdhāyām abhro bhavati //
22.1.27.a.d: तस्यै वा एतस्या एकम् एवादेवयजनं यद् आलब्धायाम् अभ्रो भवति ॥
22.1.27.a.m:
For that very one, this alone is an unfit place for sacrifice: that when she is immolated, a cloud appears.

If a cloud should appear when she is immolated, he should either cast her entirely into water, or consume all [of her].

22.1.28.a.s: yad ālabdhāyām abhraḥ syād apsu vā praveśayet sarvāṃ vā prāśnīyāt //
22.1.28.a.d: यद् आलब्धायाम् अभ्रः स्याद् अप्सु वा प्रवेशयेत् सर्वां वा प्राश्नीयात् ॥

22.1.29.a.m: The Jayas, the Abhyātānas, and the Rāṣṭrabhṛts are explained by the Brāhmaṇa.

22.1.30.a.s: cittaṃ ca svāhā \ cittiś ca svāhā \\ iti jayāñ juhoti / cittāya svāhā \ cittaye svāhā \\ iti vā //
22.1.30.a.d: चित्तं च स्वाहा \ चित्तिश् च स्वाहा \\ इति जयाञ् जुहोति । चित्ताय स्वाहा \ चित्तये स्वाहा \\ इति वा ॥
22.1.30.a.m: He offers the Jayas with: 'To thought, svāhā! And to attention, svāhā!' or with: 'To thought, svāhā! To attention, svāhā!'

22.1.31.a.s: agnir bhūtānām adhipatiḥ sa māvatu \\ ity abhyātānān asmin brahmann asmin kṣatre \\ ity abhyātāneṣv anuṣajati / pitaraḥ pitāmahās \\ iti prācīnāvītī juhoty upatiṣṭhate vā \\ ṛtāṣāḍ ṛtadhāma \\ iti rāṣṭrabhṛtaḥ / paryāyam anudrutya tasmai svāhā \\ iti pūrvāmāhutiṃ juhoti / tābhyaḥ svāhā \\ ity uttarām //
22.1.31.a.d: अग्निर् भूतानाम् अधिपतिः स मावतु \\ इत्य् अभ्यातानान् अस्मिन् ब्रह्मन्न् अस्मिन् क्षत्रे \\ इत्य् अभ्यातानेष्व् अनुषजति । पितरः पितामहास् \\ इति प्राचीनावीती जुहोत्य् उपतिष्ठते वा \\ ऋताषाड् ऋतधाम \\ इति राष्ट्रभृतः । पर्यायम् अनुद्रुत्य तस्मै स्वाहा \\ इति पूर्वामाहुतिं जुहोति । ताभ्यः स्वाहा \\ इत्य् उत्तराम् ॥
22.1.31.a.m: He connects the Abhyātānas [beginning with] 'Agni is the lord of beings, may he protect me' with [the phrase] 'in this sacred lore, in this temporal power' among the Abhyātānas. Wearing the sacred cord over the right shoulder, he offers or attends with: 'O fathers, grandfathers...' [He recites] the Rāṣṭrabhṛts: 'Conquering in truth, possessing true abode...' Having recited the turn, he offers the first oblation with: 'To him, svāhā!' and the second with: 'To them, svāhā!'

22.2.1.a.s: kāmyābhir iṣṭibhir amāvāsyāṃ paurṇamāsīṃ vā sam̐sthāpya yajeta / tā brāhmaṇavyākhyātāḥ //
22.2.1.a.d: काम्याभिर् इष्टिभिर् अमावास्यां पौर्णमासीं वा सम्̐स्थाप्य यजेत । ता ब्राह्मणव्याख्याताः ॥
22.2.1.a.m: Having concluded the New Moon rite or the Full Moon rite, he should sacrifice with optional rites; these are explained by the Brāhmaṇa.

22.2.2.a.s: sadyaskālā upām̐śutantrā yathāprakṛti caikā dakṣiṇāḥ sāṃnāyyavatyas tu dvyahakālāḥ //
22.2.2.a.d: सद्यस्काला उपाम्̐शुतन्त्रा यथाप्रकृति चैका दक्षिणाः सांनाय्यवत्यस् तु द्व्यहकालाः ॥
22.2.2.a.m: Their performance is accomplished on the same day, having the inaudible sacrificial framework, and according to the basic paradigm their sacrificial gifts are one each; but those involving the curd-and-milk oblation are accomplished over two days.

22.2.3.a.m: Between the verse containing the word 'samidhyamāna' and the verse containing the word 'samiddha', two insertion verses containing the word 'pṛthupājas' are inserted.

22.2.4.a.s: anupadāv ājyabhāgau yatkāmeṣṭis tatpravādau syātāṃ tadarthatvāt taddevatau prākṛtau vānādeśe prakṛtiḥ pratyetavyā tvāṃ citraśravastama \\ ity anuṣṭubhau saṃyājye //
22.2.4.a.d: अनुपदाव् आज्यभागौ यत्कामेष्टिस् तत्प्रवादौ स्यातां तदर्थत्वात् तद्देवतौ प्राकृतौ वानादेशे प्रकृतिः प्रत्येतव्या त्वां चित्रश्रवस्तम \\ इत्य् अनुष्टुभौ संयाज्ये ॥
22.2.4.a.m: The two clarified butter portions should be relevant, having declarations of that which the wish-fulfilling sacrifice is for, since they have that purpose; or they should have those deities, or they should be the archetypal ones; in the absence of instruction, the archetype is to be followed. The two concluding offering verses are in the anuṣṭubh metre: 'You, of most brilliant renown...'

22.2.5.a.m: The introductory verse has its distinctive mark in front, and the offering verse has its distinctive mark at the end; or vice versa.

22.2.6.a.s: aindrāgnam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet \\ iti tāsām ubhā vām indrāgnī iti catasro yājyānuvākyā dve pūrvāsāṃ tisṛṇāṃ dve uttarāsām evam ata ūrdhvaṃ karmātireke samaśaḥ prativibhajya pūrvāpūrvāsām uttarottarāsāṃ mantrātireke 'vaśiṣṭā vikalpārthā upahomā vā //
22.2.6.a.d: ऐन्द्राग्नम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपेत् \\ इति तासाम् उभा वाम् इन्द्राग्नी इति चतस्रो याज्यानुवाक्या द्वे पूर्वासां तिसृणां द्वे उत्तरासाम् एवम् अत ऊर्ध्वं कर्मातिरेके समशः प्रतिविभज्य पूर्वापूर्वासाम् उत्तरोत्तरासां मन्त्रातिरेके ऽवशिष्टा विकल्पार्था उपहोमा वा ॥
22.2.6.a.m: In 'He should assign an eleven-pot-sherd [sacrificial cake] to Indra and Agni,' of these, 'Both of you, Indra and Agni...' are the four introductory and offering verses: two for the first three [rites], two for the latter ones.
