23.1.47.a.d: आश्विनस्य यूषेण कुष्ठिकां शफं च पूरयित्वा सीसेन तन्त्रम् इत्य् अष्टर्चेन प्रतिमन्त्रं द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्यां कुष्ठिकाशफाभ्यां जुहुयात् । उत्तमायाम्̐ शृङ्गे अनुषजति । हुत्वाहुत्वा स्वेष्व् अभिषेचनपात्रेषु संपातान् अवनीयाहवनीये कुष्ठिकशफान् प्रविध्यति । एवम् उत्तरेणाष्टर्चेन सारस्वतस्य । सर्वेणानुवाकेनैन्द्रस्य ॥
23.1.47.a.m: Having filled a dewclaw and a hoof with the broth of the [victim] sacred to the Aśvins, he should offer with each mantra of the eight-verse hymn, "The web with lead...", with two dewclaws and hooves each time. At the last [verse], he fastens [them] onto the two horns. Having offered each time, having poured the residues into their respective sprinkling vessels, he casts the dewclaws and hooves into the āhavanīya fire. In this manner, [he offers] that of the [victim] sacred to Sarasvatī with the subsequent eight-verse hymn; [and] that of the [victim] sacred to Indra with the entire section.

23.1.48.a.s: audumbary āsandy aratnimātraśīrṣaṇy ānūcyā nābhidaghnapādā mauñjavivānā mitro 'si \ varuṇo 'si \\ iti tāṃ yajamānāyatane pratiṣṭhāpayati //
23.1.48.a.d: औदुम्बर्य् आसन्द्य् अरत्निमात्रशीर्षण्य् आनूच्या नाभिदघ्नपादा मौञ्जविवाना मित्रो ऽसि \ वरुणो ऽसि \\ इति तां यजमानायतने प्रतिष्ठापयति ॥
23.1.48.a.m: A throne-seat of udumbara wood, a cubit long in its head-piece and crossbars, with legs reaching up to the navel, woven with muñja grass—he sets it down in the seat of the sacrificer with: "You are Mitra; you are Varuṇa."

23.1.49.a.m: The placing, sitting upon, and addressing [of the throne-seat] are as in the Rājasūya.

23.1.50.a.s: tasyāṃ prāṅmukham āsīnaṃ pratyaṅmukhas tiṣṭhann āśvinasaṃpātair abhiṣiñcati / devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām aśvinor bhaiṣajyena tejase brahmavarcasenābhiṣiñcāmi \\ iti //
23.1.50.a.d: तस्यां प्राङ्मुखम् आसीनं प्रत्यङ्मुखस् तिष्ठन्न् आश्विनसंपातैर् अभिषिञ्चति । देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याम् अश्विनोर् भैषज्येन तेजसे ब्रह्मवर्चसेनाभिषिञ्चामि \\ इति ॥
23.1.50.a.m: Standing facing west, he consecrates [the sacrificer] seated upon it facing east with the residues of the [victim] sacred to the Aśvins, [saying]: "At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the healing medicine of the Aśvins, I consecrate you for brilliance, for spiritual luster."

23.1.51.a.m: In this manner, with the subsequent mantra, [he consecrates him with the residues] of that sacred to Sarasvatī; with the last [mantra], with those of that sacred to Indra.

23.1.52.a.s: ko 'si \ katamo 'si \\ iti pāṇī saṃmṛśyādhvaryur vyāhṛtīr japitvātra rājasūyavan maṅgalyanāmna āhūya śiro me śrīr iti yathāliṅgam aṅgāni saṃmṛśya jaṅghābhyāṃ padbhyām iti pratyavaruhya prati kṣatre pratitiṣṭhāmi rāṣṭre \\ iti japitvā trayā devās \\ ity āhutīr hutvā lomāni prayatir mama \\ iti yathāliṅgam aṅgāni saṃmṛśate //
23.1.52.a.d: को ऽसि \ कतमो ऽसि \\ इति पाणी संमृश्याध्वर्युर् व्याहृतीर् जपित्वात्र राजसूयवन् मङ्गल्यनाम्न आहूय शिरो मे श्रीर् इति यथालिङ्गम् अङ्गानि संमृश्य जङ्घाभ्यां पद्भ्याम् इति प्रत्यवरुह्य प्रति क्षत्रे प्रतितिष्ठामि राष्ट्रे \\ इति जपित्वा त्रया देवास् \\ इत्य् आहुतीर् हुत्वा लोमानि प्रयतिर् मम \\ इति यथालिङ्गम् अङ्गानि संमृशते ॥
23.1.52.a.m: Having touched both hands with: "Who are you? Which one are you?", and having muttered the mystical utterances, the adhvaryu here summons those with auspicious names as in the Rājasūya; having touched his limbs in accordance with the distinctive marks with: "My head is fortune..."; having stepped down with: "With my shanks, with my feet..."; having muttered: "I establish myself firmly in the realm, in the kingdom..."; having offered oblations with: "The three gods..."; [the sacrificer] touches his limbs according to the distinctive marks with: "My hairs are the impulse...".

23.1.53.a.m: From the Sviṣṭakṛt offering onward, [the rite is] the same up to the purificatory bath.

23.1.54.a.s: yad devā devaheḍanam ity avabhṛthe pañcāhutīr juhotīty āśmarathyaḥ / āhavanīye hūyerann ity ālekhanaḥ //
23.1.54.a.d: यद् देवा देवहेडनम् इत्य् अवभृथे पञ्चाहुतीर् जुहोतीत्य् आश्मरथ्यः । आहवनीये हूयेरन्न् इत्य् आलेखनः ॥
23.1.54.a.m: "He offers five oblations at the purificatory bath with: 'Whatever god-insult, O gods...'", says Āśmarathya. "They should be offered in the āhavanīya fire," says Ālekhana.

23.1.55.a.s: avabhṛtha nicaṅkuṇa \\ ity avabhṛthaṃ yajamāno 'bhimantrya sumitrā na āpas \\ drupadād iven mumucānas \\ ity āplutya \\ ud vayaṃ tamasas pari \\ ity ādityam upasthāya pratiyuto varuṇasya pāśas \\ ity udakāntaṃ pratyasyati //
23.1.55.a.d: अवभृथ निचङ्कुण \\ इत्य् अवभृथं यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्र्य सुमित्रा न आपस् \\ द्रुपदाद् इवेन् मुमुचानस् \\ इत्य् आप्लुत्य \\ उद् वयं तमसस् परि \\ इत्य् आदित्यम् उपस्थाय प्रतियुतो वरुणस्य पाशस् \\ इत्य् उदकान्तं प्रत्यस्यति ॥
23.1.55.a.m: Having addressed the purificatory bath with: "O purificatory bath, moving downward...", having bathed with: "May the waters be friendly to us..." [and] "As if freed from the wooden post...", having worshipped the sun with: "Looking up above the darkness...", the sacrificer casts [a twig] toward the water's edge with: "Unloosed is the fetter of Varuṇa."

23.1.56.a.m: The kindling-sticks and the worship are as in an animal sacrifice.

23.1.57.a.s: samāvavarti \\ ity upasthāya bhūḥ svāhā \\ ity āhutiṃ hutvā pūrvavatpitṛyajñaḥ //
23.1.57.a.d: समाववर्ति \\ इत्य् उपस्थाय भूः स्वाहा \\ इत्य् आहुतिं हुत्वा पूर्ववत्पितृयज्ञः ॥
23.1.57.a.m: Having worshipped with: "It has turned completely...", having offered an oblation with: "Bhūḥ svāhā!", the ancestral sacrifice is as before.

23.1.58.a.s: indrāya vayodhase paśum ālabheta / ṛṣabho dakṣiṇā //
23.1.58.a.d: इन्द्राय वयोधसे पशुम् आलभेत । ऋषभो दक्षिणा ॥
23.1.58.a.m: He should seize an animal victim for Indra, the bestower of vitality. A bull is the dakṣiṇā.
